The security team mandates that inbound traffic from the public internet must be filtered for common web exploits, cross-site scripting, and SQL injection before it reaches the load balancer, while also ensuring that the protection rules are automatically updated and centrally managed across a fleet of AWS accounts.

options.text: Deploy AWS WAF on an Application Load Balancer and associate managed rule groups for common web vulnerabilities.
Modify VPC Network Access Control Lists to drop HTTP requests containing known malicious query parameters.
Install an open-source intrusion detection system on every EC2 instance and analyze web server access logs via Amazon CloudWatch.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty with custom IP set filters to block malicious IP addresses at the VPC subnet level.

questions.explanation: AWS WAF provides layer 7 protection by inspecting HTTP and HTTPS requests. When deployed in front of an Application Load Balancer, it allows security teams to utilize AWS Managed Rules or custom rules to mitigate application-layer threats.

wrongOptionNotes.B: NACLs operate at the subnet level on IP addresses and ports, and they cannot inspect layer 7 HTTP payloads or filter SQL injection strings.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on host-based detection is reactive and places a heavy management burden on administrators without preventing attacks at the edge.
wrongOptionNotes.D: GuardDuty is a threat detection service that monitors for malicious behavior using machine learning and threat intelligence, not a web application firewall that inspects HTTP request payloads.

questions.question: A financial services company is implementing a centralized logging architecture across 50 AWS accounts using AWS Organizations. The security team requires that all Amazon CloudTrail logs delivered to a central Amazon S3 bucket cannot be modified or deleted by any user, including root accounts, for a mandatory retention period of 7 years.

options.text: Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a legal hold and configure bucket versioning.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition log files to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Archive and enable MFA Delete on the bucket.
Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance mode on the central S3 bucket and assign an IAM policy with Deny permissions on DeleteObject.
Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period of 7 years on the central S3 bucket.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode ensures strict write-once-read-many (WORM) storage. Once locked, neither AWS nor any user can delete the protected objects until the retention period expires.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Legal holds are designed for temporary investigative holds rather than fixed compliance retention periods, and Object Lock in Compliance mode should be set with a retention period instead.
wrongOptionNotes.B: MFA Delete protects against accidental deletion using multi-factor authentication, but it does not enforce a compliance-mode retention period that prevents programmatic deletion.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Governance mode allows users with specific IAM permissions to bypass retention periods, which violates the strict compliance requirement that no user can modify or delete logs.

questions.question: An internal applications team is developing a microservices architecture on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. A service running in a private subnet needs to securely retrieve sensitive database credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager without exposing the secret values in environment variables or container definition logs.

options.text: Configure the container application to call AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store directly using an IAM user access key hardcoded into the application code.
Inject the secret values directly into the task definition environment variables by referencing the Secrets Manager ARN.
Store the database credentials in a plain text configuration file within the Docker container image built in an Amazon ECR repository.
Grant the ECS task execution role permissions to read the secret and configure the task definition to inject the secret using the secrets parameter.

questions.explanation: Amazon ECS allows securely passing sensitive data to containers by referencing Secrets Manager secrets or Parameter Store parameters directly within the container definition using the task execution role.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Hardcoding IAM user access keys in application code introduces significant security risks and violates the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Injecting secrets as environment variables makes them visible in the Amazon ECS console, API responses, and potentially container logs if debugging is enabled.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Hardcoding credentials into container images violates core security best practices and exposes secrets to anyone with read access to the container image.

questions.question: A security architect is designing a centralized Identity and Access Management (IAM) strategy for an organization with multiple AWS accounts. The architect needs to ensure that developers across all accounts can assume a specific deployment role, but only from corporate network IP addresses.

options.text: Create an SCP at the organizational root level denying all API calls originating outside the corporate IP range.
Apply an Amazon S3 bucket policy to store session credentials only when accessed from trusted enterprise endpoints.
Configure an IAM trust policy on the role with a condition element specifying aws:SourceIp matching the corporate CIDR block.
Attach a permissions boundary to the IAM role that restricts access based on the source IP address.

questions.explanation: An IAM role's trust policy defines which principals can assume the role and under what conditions. Using condition keys like aws:SourceIp in the trust policy enforces network perimeter checks during role assumption.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Service Control Policies apply broadly across accounts, but restricting general API calls based on source IP can block valid AWS service-to-service internal calls.
wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 bucket policies govern access to S3 objects, not the capability of users or applications to assume cross-account IAM deployment roles.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Permissions boundaries are used to delegate permissions management while setting the maximum permissions an entity can have, not for enforcing network-perimeter access conditions.

questions.question: A healthcare enterprise stores patient health records in Amazon S3. The security team discovers that some newly uploaded objects lack proper server-side encryption. The solutions architect must implement a preventive control that automatically denies any S3 PutObject request that does not specify AWS KMS encryption.

options.text: Configure an Amazon S3 Lifecycle rule to encrypt unencrypted objects every 24 hours after upload.
Apply an Amazon S3 bucket policy with a Deny effect for PutObject requests when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is missing or not set to aws:kms.
Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket using Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
Deploy AWS Trusted Advisor to flag unencrypted buckets during daily security posture scans.

questions.explanation: S3 bucket policies can use condition keys such as `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` to enforce that clients supply specific encryption parameters on every upload request.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Lifecycle rules cannot enforce immediate preventive encryption upon upload; they operate asynchronously and leave a window of vulnerability.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Default encryption applies a fallback encryption method if none is provided, but it does not deny requests that explicitly try to bypass or omit encryption headers depending on configuration.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Trusted Advisor provides detective controls and notifications, whereas the requirement calls for an immediate preventive control.

questions.question: An enterprise maintains a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances running a mission-critical billing application in a private VPC subnet. To comply with internal security audits, all instances must be continuously monitored for unauthorized network connections, anomalous API activity, and potential malware infections without installing third-party agent software.

options.text: Write custom scripts using AWS Lambda to parse CloudWatch Logs every minute and flag abnormal IP addresses.
Install Amazon Inspector agents on every EC2 instance to perform real-time network packet inspection and malware scanning.
Enable Amazon GuardDuty, AWS CloudTrail, and Amazon VPC Flow Logs across the AWS account.
Configure AWS WAF on an internal Application Load Balancer sitting in front of the billing instances.

questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a managed threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior by analyzing multiple AWS data sources like CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Building a custom log parsing system reinvents the functionality provided natively and securely by Amazon GuardDuty.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Amazon Inspector evaluates software vulnerabilities and network reachability, but GuardDuty is the primary service for continuous threat detection across network and log telemetry.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS WAF filters web application traffic (Layer 7), but it does not monitor overall EC2 instance network behavior, OS anomalies, or API calls.

questions.question: A financial corporation requires that all Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes created across its entire AWS organization must be encrypted by default. Furthermore, developers must not be able to disable encryption or select unapproved encryption keys when launching new Amazon EC2 instances.

options.text: Enable EBS encryption by default in all AWS accounts and regions, and use a custom AWS KMS customer managed key.
Create an IAM policy for each developer that removes the ec2:CreateVolume permission and forces them to use CloudFormation.
Rely on developers to manually check the encryption box in the EC2 launch wizard for each volume.
Configure Amazon S3 bucket policies to inspect EBS volume snapshots upon creation.

questions.explanation: Enabling EBS encryption by default at the account and region level guarantees that all newly created volumes and snapshots are encrypted automatically without depending on manual user selection.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Removing create volume permissions hinders operational agility, and developers could still launch instances with unencrypted root volumes through auto-scaling or direct console use.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on manual developer actions fails compliance mandates because human error can lead to unencrypted volumes.
wrongOptionNotes.D: EBS snapshots and volumes are separate from Amazon S3 buckets; S3 bucket policies do not apply to EBS volume encryption settings.

questions.question: An organization is deploying a public-facing web application on AWS. The security team mandates that the application must be protected against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, and any traffic spikes or volumetric attacks must be mitigated automatically with financial protection against infrastructure downtime costs.

options.text: Deploy NAT Gateways across multiple Availability Zones to absorb incoming volumetric UDP reflection attacks.
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and associate it with the Application Load Balancer and Amazon CloudFront distributions.
Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to automatically scale down Auto Scaling groups when incoming requests exceed normal baselines.
Rely exclusively on AWS Shield Standard and create custom AWS WAF rate-limiting rules for every IP address.

questions.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced provides advanced threat protection for applications running on AWS, including 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team and financial protection against DDoS-driven spikes in AWS usage fees.

wrongOptionNotes.A: NAT Gateways are designed for outbound internet access from private subnets, not for mitigating DDoS attacks against public endpoints.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Scaling down during a traffic spike or DDoS attack would cause immediate denial of service for legitimate users.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS Shield Standard protects against common layer 3 and 4 attacks automatically, but it does not provide 24/7 DRT support or financial reimbursement for scaling costs during large volumetric attacks.

questions.question: A security engineer is conducting an access review for an enterprise AWS environment. The auditor notes that an IAM role used by a third-party audit tool has broad permissions (`AdministratorAccess`). The architect must restrict this role so that it can only perform read-only actions and can only be assumed during standard business hours (9 AM to 5 PM UTC).

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket policy that blocks read requests outside of business hours.
Configure Amazon Cognito user pools to authenticate the third-party auditors before granting them access to the IAM role.
Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) to the entire organization denying all write operations outside of business hours.
Attach the AWS managed policy ReadOnlyAccess to the role, and add a condition to the role's trust policy using date and time functions such as `aws:CurrentTime`.

questions.explanation: Least privilege is achieved by scoping permissions down to ReadOnlyAccess, and time-based access control for role assumption is implemented using condition keys (e.g., `aws:CurrentTime`) in the IAM role's trust policy.

wrongOptionNotes.A: S3 bucket policies govern access to S3 storage, not general AWS API permissions or role assumption times across other AWS services.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Cognito handles user authentication for web and mobile apps, whereas IAM role assumption is handled via AWS STS and trust policies.
wrongOptionNotes.C: SCPs apply to accounts, not specific roles, and timing restrictions are best handled in the role's trust policy condition rather than account-wide SCPs.

questions.question: An enterprise developer accidentally committed an IAM user's long-term access key and secret access key into a public source code repository. Security operations identified the leak within minutes. What is the most immediate and effective action the security engineer must take to mitigate potential unauthorized access?

options.text: Delete the public GitHub repository and wait for web crawlers to index the removal.
Change the root user password of the AWS account and enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
Attach an Amazon S3 bucket policy to deny public access across all buckets in the account.
Deactivate or delete the compromised IAM access key immediately in the AWS IAM console.

questions.explanation: When an IAM access key is compromised, immediate deactivation or deletion of the key in IAM is the primary step to terminate active sessions and prevent unauthorized API calls.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Deleting the repository does not invalidate the leaked keys, which may have already been harvested by automated bots.
wrongOptionNotes.B: The leak involved an IAM user access key, not the root user credentials. Changing the root password does not affect IAM user keys.
wrongOptionNotes.C: S3 bucket policies do not invalidate compromised IAM user credentials that could be used across many different AWS services.

questions.question: A financial institution is deploying a highly sensitive database on Amazon RDS PostgreSQL. Compliance regulations mandate that the database storage must be encrypted, and the encryption keys must be managed in AWS KMS using a dedicated key that is automatically rotated annually, with strict access logging.

options.text: Store unencrypted data in RDS and rely on application-level encryption using hardcoded certificates inside the database.
Configure Amazon RDS encryption using an AWS managed key (aws/rds).
Enable Amazon RDS storage encryption using a Customer Managed Key (CMK) in AWS KMS with annual key rotation enabled.
Use Amazon S3 client-side encryption to encrypt RDS backups before they are transferred to storage.

questions.explanation: Customer Managed Keys in AWS KMS provide organizations with complete control over encryption keys used by Amazon RDS, including key policies, auditing, and automatic annual key rotation.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Application-level encryption with hardcoded keys is insecure and does not meet database storage compliance mandates.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS managed keys are managed by AWS on behalf of the user and do not support customer control over annual key rotation schedules or fine-grained key policies.
wrongOptionNotes.D: RDS storage encryption protects active database volumes directly, and client-side S3 encryption does not fulfill RDS storage encryption requirements.

questions.question: A multinational corporation uses AWS Organizations to manage over 100 AWS accounts. The corporate security team needs to enforce a mandatory guardrail ensuring that no developer or administrator in any member account can disable AWS CloudTrail logging or delete logging configuration.

options.text: Create individual IAM policies for every user across all 100 accounts that deny CloudTrail deletion permissions.
Deploy Amazon CloudWatch alarms in each account to send an email notification whenever CloudTrail is stopped.
Configure an S3 bucket policy on the centralized logging bucket to block all write requests.
Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the organizational unit or root level that explicitly denies `cloudtrail:DeleteTrail` and `cloudtrail:StopLogging`.

questions.explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations enable security architects to establish mandatory preventive guardrails across multiple accounts, restricting actions such as disabling CloudTrail.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Managing individual IAM policies across hundreds of accounts is prone to human error and administrative overhead, and users with sufficient privileges could modify them.
wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudWatch alarms provide detective notifications after an action occurs, whereas the requirement is a preventive guardrail to stop the action entirely.
wrongOptionNotes.C: An S3 bucket policy blocks writes to the bucket, but it does not prevent a user from stopping or deleting the CloudTrail trail definition within the AWS account.

questions.question: An enterprise web application running on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets needs to download operating system patches from external repositories. The security team mandates that outbound internet access must be restricted to specific approved patch repository domains, and instances must not have direct public IP addresses.

options.text: Configure VPC Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) to allow traffic only to the IP addresses of the patch repositories.
Attach Elastic IP addresses to every EC2 instance and configure security group outbound rules to block unauthorized IPs.
Disable all outbound security group rules and rely on Amazon S3 VPC endpoints for all operating system patches.
Route outbound traffic through a NAT Gateway and integrate AWS Network Firewall to inspect and filter traffic based on domain names.

questions.explanation: AWS Network Firewall allows security teams to inspect and filter outbound traffic from private VPC subnets based on fully qualified domain names (FQDNs), ensuring compliance when instances need access to external update repositories.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Patch repository IP addresses change frequently and dynamically, making static IP-based NACL rules operationally infeasible for domain filtering.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Attaching Elastic IPs gives instances direct public internet exposure, violating the requirement to prevent direct public IP addresses.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Operating system vendor repositories (like Ubuntu or RedHat update servers) are external to AWS and cannot be reached solely via Amazon S3 VPC endpoints.

questions.question: An auditor discovers that a production Amazon S3 bucket containing sensitive customer Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is publicly accessible via internet-routable URLs. The solutions architect needs to immediately implement a safeguard that blocks all public access at the account level across all current and future S3 buckets.

options.text: Attach an IAM permissions boundary to all developer users denying s3:PutBucketPolicy.
Configure an AWS WAF web ACL to block requests originating from unauthorized public IP ranges.
Manually update the bucket ACL on every individual S3 bucket to remove public read permissions.
Enable Amazon S3 Block Public Access at the AWS account level.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Block Public Access provides centralized controls to prevent public access to S3 buckets. Enabling these settings at the account level ensures that no bucket in the account can ever be made public.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Permissions boundaries restrict user roles, but they do not actively remediate existing public S3 bucket configurations or enforce global S3 blocking.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS WAF protects endpoints like Application Load Balancers and CloudFront distributions, but it does not control direct HTTPS access to Amazon S3 buckets.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Manual updates are slow, prone to oversight, and do not provide a preventive guardrail for future buckets created in the account.

questions.question: A financial technology company deploys an AWS Lambda function that processes customer financial transactions and interacts with an Amazon DynamoDB table. The security team requires that the Lambda function execution role adheres strictly to the principle of least privilege, granting access only to the specific DynamoDB table required for transactions.

options.text: Configure the Lambda function to run without any execution role and rely on the default account root credentials.
Attach the AWS managed policy `AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess` to the Lambda execution role.
Grant the Lambda function administrator privileges by attaching `AdministratorAccess` for ease of troubleshooting.
Attach a custom inline IAM policy to the Lambda execution role that limits actions (such as GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem) to the specific Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation: Least privilege requires restricting IAM policies to specific actions and explicit resource ARNs (such as a specific DynamoDB table ARN) rather than using broad managed policies.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS Lambda functions require an execution role to assume permissions; running without one will result in immediate authorization failures.
wrongOptionNotes.B: `AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess` grants broad permissions across all DynamoDB tables in the account, violating the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.C: `AdministratorAccess` provides unrestricted access to all AWS services and resources, representing a severe security risk.

questions.question: An enterprise web application running on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets requires internet access to download software patches. To comply with strict security standards, the traffic must never traverse the public internet, and the architecture must minimize operational overhead and cost.

options.text: Attach an Elastic IP directly to each private EC2 instance to facilitate secure, encrypted direct internet access.
Deploy an AWS Transit Gateway connected to a NAT Gateway in a public subnet to route traffic privately.
Configure an AWS Gateway VPC Endpoint for Amazon S3 and interface endpoints for other required services.
Deploy a fleet of proxy EC2 instances in a public subnet to securely forward private subnet internet traffic.

questions.explanation: Amazon VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink and Gateway Endpoints) allow resources within a private subnet to communicate with supported AWS services and VPC endpoint services privately, keeping traffic entirely within the Amazon network and eliminating NAT Gateway or internet gateway requirements.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Elastic IPs cannot be directly attached to instances in private subnets, and this would expose instances directly to the public internet.
wrongOptionNotes.B: A NAT Gateway still routes traffic over the public internet, failing the security requirement, and adds unnecessary cost.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Managing proxy EC2 instances introduces heavy operational overhead and ongoing compute costs compared to native serverless AWS VPC endpoints.

questions.question: A financial enterprise is designing a multi-tier application on AWS. Compliance policies dictate that all data stored in Amazon EBS volumes attached to production EC2 instances must be encrypted at rest using keys managed and rotated annually by the security team. The solution must enforce this across all current and future accounts.

options.text: Rely on developers to manually specify custom encryption keys when launching instances via AWS CloudFormation templates.
Write a custom AWS Lambda function that triggers every hour to find unencrypted volumes and delete them.
Use Amazon Macie to continuously scan EBS volumes and apply encryption retroactively after creation.
Enforce encryption by default for all new Amazon EBS volumes in all regions using AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMKs), and use AWS Organizations SCPs to prevent unencrypted volume creation.

questions.explanation: To meet strict compliance mandates, organizations should enable EBS encryption by default at the region level and enforce preventative guardrails using AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Relying on manual developer configuration introduces a high risk of human error and non-compliance.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Reactive remediation via deletion causes service disruption and is not a preventative security control.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Amazon Macie cannot retroactively encrypt EBS volumes; it only discovers and reports sensitive data.

questions.question: An organization is deploying a public-facing web application on AWS behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team mandates that the application must be protected against common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, while also allowing custom rate-based rules to mitigate DDoS attacks.

options.text: Use AWS Trusted Advisor security checks to automatically block incoming malicious IP addresses in the security groups.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty with a custom threat list to monitor and block HTTP flood attacks at the load balancer.
Deploy AWS WAF and associate a web ACL containing managed rules and rate-based rules directly with the Application Load Balancer.
Implement AWS Shield Advanced on the EC2 instances and write custom iptables rules to block malicious payloads.

questions.explanation: AWS WAF allows you to monitor HTTP(S) requests forwarded to an Application Load Balancer, Amazon API Gateway, or Amazon CloudFront, protecting web applications against web exploits and bots using customizable rules.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations and does not actively remediate or block live traffic at the application layer.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes AWS CloudTrail logs, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs, not inline web traffic.
wrongOptionNotes.D: iptables rules on EC2 instances cannot efficiently inspect Layer 7 web traffic payloads compared to an edge web application firewall.

questions.question: A security engineer is auditing an enterprise AWS environment. The review reveals that an IAM role used by an automated deployment pipeline has overly permissive permissions (AdministratorAccess). The security team needs to immediately restrict this role's effective permissions without modifying the underlying IAM managed policy directly, as it is shared with other pipelines.

options.text: Modify the trust policy of the IAM role to restrict the times during which the pipeline can assume the role.
Enable AWS CloudTrail log analysis to block API calls made by the deployment pipeline that exceed standard deployment scope.
Attach a permissions boundary to the IAM role that limits its maximum possible permissions.
Delete the AdministratorAccess policy from AWS IAM entirely and recreate smaller policies.

questions.explanation: IAM permissions boundaries are managed policies that set the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant to an entity. They are ideal for delegating permissions or restricting overly broad roles shared across resources.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Trust policies control who can assume a role, not what actions the role can perform once assumed.
wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudTrail is a logging service and does not provide active, inline prevention of API execution.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Deleting a managed policy affects all other entities sharing that policy, violating the requirement not to impact other pipelines.

questions.question: A healthcare enterprise stores patient health records in Amazon S3 buckets. The security team discovers that some newly uploaded objects lack server-side encryption headers. The solution must guarantee that all objects uploaded to the S3 bucket are automatically encrypted using AWS KMS, rejecting any unencrypted upload attempts.

options.text: Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket using Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
Set up an AWS WAF rule to inspect PUT requests to the S3 bucket and insert encryption headers automatically.
Apply an Amazon S3 bucket policy with a condition requiring the 's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption' header to be present and set to 'aws:kms'.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that triggers an AWS Lambda function to encrypt unencrypted S3 objects immediately after upload.

questions.explanation: To enforce encryption on all S3 uploads, you can use an S3 bucket policy that denies any 's3:PutObject' requests unless the correct server-side encryption header is specified in the API call.

wrongOptionNotes.A: The requirement mandates AWS KMS encryption, not default S3-managed keys.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS WAF cannot inspect or modify traffic destined directly for Amazon S3 endpoints in this manner.
wrongOptionNotes.D: This is a reactive approach; objects exist unencrypted for a brief window between upload and Lambda execution.

questions.question: A multinational corporation uses AWS Organizations to manage over 100 AWS accounts. The corporate security team requires that no resources, specifically Amazon EC2 instances, can be launched outside of two specific AWS regions (us-east-1 and eu-west-1) across any current or future account.

options.text: Configure individual IAM policies for every user and role across all 100 accounts to restrict region usage.
Configure AWS Trusted Advisor alerts to notify the security team whenever an EC2 instance is launched in an unauthorized region.
Write a centralized AWS CloudTrail event notification that triggers an AWS Lambda function to terminate unauthorized EC2 instances.
Apply an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) at the root level that denies EC2 actions in all regions except us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

questions.explanation: AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) provide centralized control over the maximum available permissions for all accounts in your organization, making them the ideal tool for enforcing region restrictions organization-wide.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Managing individual IAM policies across 100 accounts introduces massive administrative overhead and is prone to human error.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Trusted Advisor alerts are reactive and do not prevent the creation of resources in unauthorized regions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Reactive termination leaves a window of vulnerability and can disrupt business operations unpredictably.

questions.question: An enterprise developer accidentally committed an IAM user's long-term access key and secret access key into a public code repository. The security team needs to identify if these credentials were used maliciously and ensure ongoing monitoring for exposed credentials across GitHub.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon CloudWatch alarm based on standard CPU utilization metrics of the root account.
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor to scan public code repositories daily for leaked AWS credentials.
Run AWS Config rules to check if the compromised IAM user has active console passwords enabled.
Activate Amazon GuardDuty to detect unauthorized behavior and use AWS IAM Access Analyzer to review external access.

questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty continuously monitors AWS environments for malicious or unauthorized behavior (such as unusual API calls using leaked keys), while tools like IAM Access Analyzer help secure resource policies.

wrongOptionNotes.A: CPU utilization metrics are unrelated to IAM credential leaks or API activity monitoring.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS Trusted Advisor does not scan external code repositories for leaked secrets.
wrongOptionNotes.C: AWS Config rules evaluate resource configurations, not whether API credentials have been leaked on external platforms.

questions.question: A financial institution runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that all transport-layer communications from clients to the load balancer must use strong cipher suites and enforce TLS 1.3 where possible, with centralized certificate management.

options.text: Configure Amazon CloudFront to terminate TLS and forward unencrypted traffic over the public internet to the EC2 instances.

Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to provision a public certificate, and configure the Application Load Balancer listener with a modern predefined security policy (e.g., ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06).
Install self-signed SSL certificates directly onto each EC2 instance and configure local web server encryption.
Store private keys in plaintext inside an Amazon S3 bucket and download them onto the ALB during boot.

questions.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) simplifies provisioning and managing SSL/TLS certificates, while Application Load Balancers support customizable security policies that define strict cipher suites and TLS protocol versions.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Forwarding unencrypted traffic over the public internet violates security compliance standards for financial applications.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Self-signed certificates are untrusted by browsers, and decentralized certificate management creates significant operational overhead.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Storing private keys in plaintext in S3 is a critical security vulnerability.

questions.question: An enterprise operates a multi-tenant web application on Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC. The security team mandates that traffic between instances belonging to different application tiers must be strictly isolated at the network level, even if they reside within the same subnet.

options.text: Rely on Linux OS-level iptables rules configured manually on each individual EC2 instance.
Deploy an AWS Transit Gateway between every single EC2 instance to inspect all intra-VPC traffic.
Use Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones to block DNS resolution between isolated application tiers.
Configure Amazon VPC Security Groups with least-privilege ingress and egress rules referencing other security groups.

questions.explanation: Security Groups act as a virtual firewall for your EC2 instances to control inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. By referencing other security groups, you can securely isolate tiers even if they share a subnet.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Relying on OS-level configurations is prone to human error, difficult to audit centrally, and does not provide robust cloud-native network isolation.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Transit Gateway connects multiple VPCs and on-premises networks; using it between instances within the same VPC is architecturally incorrect and cost-prohibitive.
wrongOptionNotes.C: DNS resolution blocking does not prevent direct IP-based network communication between instances.

questions.question: A financial services company is implementing a centralized logging architecture across 50 AWS accounts using AWS Organizations. All AWS CloudTrail logs must be aggregated into a single, highly secure Amazon S3 bucket located in a dedicated Log Archive account. The solution must prevent any user—including account administrators—from tampering with or deleting the log files.

options.text: Encrypt the S3 bucket using AWS KMS and delete the KMS key immediately after log delivery.
Enable Amazon S3 Object Lock in Governance mode on the log archive bucket and restrict IAM policies.
Configure Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period, and apply an organization-level trail via AWS CloudTrail.
Rely on standard S3 bucket versioning and daily lifecycle rules to transition logs to Glacier.

questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail organizational trails aggregate logs across all accounts into a designated S3 bucket. Utilizing Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode ensures Write Once, Read Many (WORM) storage, preventing log deletion or modification.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Deleting the KMS key prevents anyone, including audit systems, from ever reading the log files again.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Governance mode can be bypassed by users with specific IAM permissions, failing the strict anti-tampering requirement for financial logs.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Standard versioning allows users with proper permissions to permanently delete object versions, making it insufficient for tamper-proof logging.

questions.question: A financial corporation requires that all Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes created across its entire AWS organization must be encrypted automatically. The security architect needs a preventative mechanism that blocks any attempt to launch EC2 instances with unencrypted volumes.

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge to listen for EBS volume creation events and delete non-compliant volumes.
Write an AWS Config conformance pack that alerts the security team when unencrypted volumes are detected.
Instruct all cloud engineers to always check the encryption box manually in the AWS Console.
Enable EBS encryption by default in all accounts and regions, and use an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) to deny the creation of unencrypted volumes.

questions.explanation: Preventative controls in AWS Organizations utilize Service Control Policies (SCPs) combined with regional EBS encryption settings to ensure that no unencrypted storage can ever be provisioned.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Reactive deletion causes operational disruption and does not prevent the initial creation API call.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS Config provides detective controls, not preventative guardrails that block creation.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on manual user behavior is prone to human error and does not satisfy strict corporate compliance mandates.

questions.question: An organization is deploying a public-facing web application on AWS using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. To protect against unauthorized access and API scraping, the security team requires that all requests must be authenticated using JSON Web Tokens (JWT) issued by an external OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider.

options.text: Manually write custom authorization logic inside every Lambda function to decode and verify JWT signatures.
Configure an HTTP API in API Gateway with a native JWT authorizer to validate tokens before requests reach the backend Lambda functions.
Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of API Gateway and configure Lambda@Edge to perform authentication checks.
Use AWS IAM authorization for every API Gateway route and issue temporary SigV4 credentials to external web clients.

questions.explanation: Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs natively support JWT authorizers, allowing API Gateway to validate JSON Web Tokens from identity providers (such as Auth0, Okta, or Cognito) before forwarding requests to backend integrations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Writing custom validation logic in every Lambda function introduces code duplication, maintenance overhead, and security risks.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While Lambda@Edge can handle authentication, API Gateway HTTP APIs provide native built-in JWT authorization natively and more simply without edge overhead.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Issuing AWS SigV4 credentials to public web clients is insecure and impractical for consumer-facing web applications.

questions.question: A security engineer is conducting an access review for an enterprise AWS environment. The auditor notes that an IAM role used by an external third-party auditor has broad read access across multiple production S3 buckets. The security team needs to ensure that this third-party role can only assume access when connecting from the auditor's specific corporate IP address range.

options.text: Attach an AWS WAF Web ACL to the IAM service endpoint to filter incoming API requests based on IP addresses.
Modify the IAM role's trust policy to include a 'aws:SourceIp' condition restricting assumption requests to the corporate IP range.
Configure Amazon VPC Network ACLs on all private subnets to block external IP addresses.
Rely on the third-party auditor to manually configure their local VPN to match AWS security baselines.

questions.explanation: IAM role trust policies (assume role policies) can include conditional operators such as 'IpAddress' and 'StringEquals' with keys like 'aws:SourceIp' to restrict who can assume the role and from where.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS WAF cannot be attached to IAM endpoints; it protects web applications on CloudFront, ALBs, and API Gateways.
wrongOptionNotes.C: VPC Network ACLs operate at the subnet level for VPC traffic, not for global AWS IAM service API calls.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Relying on external entities for internal security enforcement violates zero-trust principles.

questions.question: A financial institution is deploying a highly sensitive database on Amazon RDS PostgreSQL. Compliance regulations mandate that database connection traffic must be encrypted in transit using SSL/TLS, and the database must reject any unencrypted connection attempts.

options.text: Enable Amazon RDS storage encryption using AWS KMS customer managed keys.
Configure an Application Load Balancer in front of the RDS database to terminate TLS connections.
Attach a VPC Security Group rule that blocks port 5432 for all unencrypted IP packets.
Modify the RDS parameter group to set the 'rds.force_ssl' parameter to '1'.

questions.explanation: Amazon RDS allows you to enforce transport-layer security by setting the 'rds.force_ssl' parameter to true (1) in the DB parameter group, ensuring that clients must connect using SSL/TLS.

wrongOptionNotes.A: RDS storage encryption protects data at rest on disk, not data in transit across network connections.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Application Load Balancers operate at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and cannot load-balance raw PostgreSQL TCP database traffic.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Security groups operate at Layer 4 and cannot inspect network payloads to determine whether an active database connection is using SSL/TLS.

questions.question: A global media company is designing a disaster recovery (DR) strategy for a critical media asset management platform hosted on AWS. The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) must be under 1 minute, and the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) must be near zero. The primary region is us-east-1, and the secondary region is us-west-2. Which DR architecture meets these requirements cost-effectively?

options.text: Set up a warm standby architecture with a scaled-down fleet of Amazon EC2 instances and a read replica of the database in the secondary region, scaling up instances only when Route 53 detects a failure.
Deploy a pilot light architecture with core database replication running continuously and compute capacity scaled down to minimum instances in the secondary region.
Implement a backup and restore strategy using AWS Backup to take daily snapshots of Amazon EBS volumes and Amazon RDS databases, copying them to us-west-2.
Implement a multi-site active-active architecture where application stacks run concurrently in both us-east-1 and us-west-2, utilizing Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing and health checks.

questions.explanation: A multi-site active-active disaster recovery strategy ensures that traffic is served concurrently from multiple AWS regions. By combining Amazon Route 53 routing policies with continuous data replication (such as Amazon Aurora Global Databases), organizations can achieve near-zero RTO and minimal RPO.

wrongOptionNotes.A: A warm standby provides an RPO under 1 minute, but the RTO involves scaling up compute capacity, which violates the near-zero RTO requirement.
wrongOptionNotes.B: A pilot light architecture provides an RPO under 1 minute using database replication, but the RTO will be minutes to hours because compute capacity must be provisioned and scaled up during a disaster.
wrongOptionNotes.C: A backup and restore approach results in an RPO of hours and an RTO of hours, failing both requirements.

questions.question: A multinational financial services firm is designing a multi-region active-passive disaster recovery strategy for its core transaction processing database hosted on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The architecture requires an RPO of zero and an RTO of less than 30 seconds. Which configuration satisfies these constraints?

options.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to continuously replicate data from an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL instance in us-east-1 to another RDS PostgreSQL instance in eu-west-1.

Configure an Aurora Global Database with the primary cluster in us-east-1 and a secondary read-replica cluster in eu-west-1. Promote the secondary cluster manually via the AWS Management Console upon failure.
Schedule automated Amazon RDS snapshots every 15 minutes in us-east-1 and copy them to eu-west-1 for restoration during an outage.
Configure an Aurora Global Database with the primary cluster in us-east-1 and a secondary cluster in eu-west-1 with managed failover enabled.

questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora Global Databases provide cross-region disaster recovery with low latency (typically under a second of replication lag for an RPO of near zero) and support managed failover to promote the secondary region rapidly, meeting strict RTO targets.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS DMS introduces replication lag and management overhead, and failover is not instantaneous or natively managed with an RTO under 30 seconds compared to Aurora Global Databases.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Manual promotion via the console introduces significant delay, violating the RTO of less than 30 seconds.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Snapshot replication every 15 minutes results in a 15-minute RPO, which fails the RPO of zero requirement.

questions.question: An e-commerce enterprise operates a globally distributed web application using Amazon CloudFront and Amazon API Gateway backed by AWS Lambda in the us-east-1 region. Due to regulatory changes, the enterprise must implement a disaster recovery strategy in eu-west-1. The recovery solution must handle regional failovers automatically without manual DNS updates. How should the Solutions Architect design this?

options.text: Set up CloudFront origin groups with a primary origin pointing to the us-east-1 API Gateway and a secondary origin pointing to the eu-west-1 API Gateway, configured with failover status codes.
Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy pointing to two separate CloudFront distributions in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
Deploy a Network Load Balancer in front of both API Gateway endpoints and configure cross-region target groups.
Configure Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller with routing controls to automatically redirect CloudFront origin requests to the eu-west-1 API Gateway during an outage.

questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront origin groups enable high availability and automated failover. By designating a primary and secondary origin, CloudFront can seamlessly route traffic to the secondary regional API Gateway if the primary origin experiences HTTP 5xx errors.

wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudFront is a global service; creating regional distributions tied to latency routing does not provide active-passive failover for origin APIs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Network Load Balancers cannot target endpoints across different AWS regions directly.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Amazon CloudFront cannot directly use Route 53 Application Recovery Controller routing controls as an origin failover mechanism without custom origin groups.

questions.question: A healthcare analytics platform stores sensitive patient data in Amazon S3. The company requires a cross-region disaster recovery replication strategy where objects and all metadata, including object tags and access control lists (ACLs), are replicated to a secondary region. Compliance requires that replication must be encrypted and handle existing objects as well as new uploads. Which solution meets these criteria?

options.text: Configure S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) with a replication rule pointing to a bucket in the secondary AWS region.
Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) enabled, ensuring replication of existing objects using S3 Batch Replication, and maintaining encryption settings.
Write a custom AWS Lambda function triggered by Amazon S3 event notifications that reads objects from the primary bucket and writes them to the secondary region bucket using SSE-S3 encryption.
Use AWS Storage Gateway in cached volume mode in the primary region to back up data to an S3 bucket in the secondary region.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) combined with S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) and S3 Batch Replication provides a fully managed, compliant solution to replicate both existing and new objects along with their metadata and encryption parameters across regions.

wrongOptionNotes.A: S3 Same-Region Replication only replicates objects within the same AWS region, not across regions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: A custom Lambda function introduces scaling limits, potential data loss during invocation failures, and high operational overhead compared to native S3 replication features.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Storage Gateway is designed for hybrid cloud storage and file/volume caching, not as a direct cross-region S3 disaster recovery replication mechanism.

questions.question: A SaaS provider runs an enterprise application on Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer in us-east-1. The company is establishing a disaster recovery site in us-west-2 using a warm standby model. The database uses Amazon Aurora Global Database. The Auto Scaling group in us-west-2 should run a minimal capacity of 2 instances during normal operations and scale up automatically when an outage occurs. Which automated mechanism should be used to trigger the scaling and traffic shift?

options.text: Configure a single Application Load Balancer spanning both us-east-1 and us-west-2 with cross-zone load balancing enabled.
Use AWS Lambda to periodically poll the health of us-east-1 instances and manually execute AWS CLI commands to update Route 53 DNS records.

Configure Amazon Route 53 health checks on the us-east-1 ALB with a failover routing policy pointing to the us-west-2 ALB, and use Amazon CloudWatch alarms in us-west-2 to adjust the Auto Scaling group desired capacity upon detecting traffic inflow.
Set up an Amazon SNS topic that triggers an AWS Systems Manager runbook to terminate instances in us-east-1 and launch instances in us-west-2.

questions.explanation: A warm standby disaster recovery model leverages Amazon Route 53 failover routing with health checks to automatically shift traffic. Once traffic arrives in the secondary region, auto scaling configurations and CloudWatch metrics can react to increase compute capacity.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Application Load Balancers are regional constructs and cannot span across multiple AWS regions.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Polling via Lambda with manual CLI updates introduces high latency and operational complexity, failing to provide an automated, resilient failover.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Relying on an SNS topic and manual intervention runbooks does not provide a robust, automated network and compute failover mechanism.

questions.question: A financial services organization is designing a multi-region active-passive disaster recovery architecture for an application running on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate. The database layer uses Amazon DynamoDB. To ensure business continuity, the DynamoDB table must be replicated globally with low latency and automated multi-region failover. Which feature should the Solutions Architect implement?

options.text: Write a scheduled AWS Lambda function using Amazon EventBridge to export DynamoDB table items to Amazon S3 and import them into the secondary region every hour.
Configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR) and restore backups manually into the secondary region during an outage.
Enable DynamoDB global tables to automatically replicate data across multiple AWS regions with active-active read and write capabilities and conflict resolution.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to continuously replicate data from a DynamoDB table in us-east-1 to a DynamoDB table in us-west-2.

questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB global tables transparently replicate data across user-specified AWS regions, providing automatic multi-region failover, local read/write performance, and an RPO/RTO close to zero without custom replication code.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Exporting and importing hourly results in a 1-hour RPO, which is unacceptable for transaction processing systems.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Restoring from PITR during an outage results in high RTO (hours) and fails active-passive recovery requirements.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS DMS is unnecessary and inefficient for DynamoDB when native global tables provide fully managed multi-region replication.

questions.question: An enterprise application hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in us-east-1 requires a disaster recovery backup stored in us-west-2. The compliance mandate states that backup recovery points must be immutable (write-once-read-many) to protect against ransomware, and backups must be retained for 7 years. Which AWS service and configuration best meet these requirements?

options.text: Store encrypted backups on Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with backup replication configured to us-west-2.
Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan with cross-region copy to us-west-2, applying an AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode.
Upload backups to an Amazon S3 bucket in us-west-2 with S3 Versioning enabled and MFA Delete configured.
Take Amazon EBS snapshots and copy them to us-west-2, then apply an IAM policy denying the 'ec2:DeleteSnapshot' permission on all users.

questions.explanation: AWS Backup Vault Lock enforces WORM (Write Once, Read Many) governance or compliance controls on backup vaults. Compliance mode ensures that no one—including the root account user—can delete the backups before the retention period expires.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Amazon EFS does not natively provide compliance-mode vault lock immutability features comparable to AWS Backup Vault Lock or S3 Object Lock.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While S3 versioning and MFA Delete protect against accidental deletion, S3 Object Lock in compliance mode is specifically designed for strict WORM immutability compliance requirements.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Relying solely on IAM policies is insufficient for strict immutability mandates because administrators with permission can modify the IAM policy itself.

questions.question: An international shipping company is designing a mission-critical tracking application on AWS that requires multi-region resilience. The application architecture includes Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. If a major AWS region outage occurs, the system must automatically reroute traffic and fail over database read and write operations with minimal latency impact. Which architectural pattern should the Solutions Architect implement?

options.text: Use AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups in us-east-1 and us-west-2 pointing to a single regional Application Load Balancer in us-east-1.
Deploy API Gateway and Lambda in both us-east-1 and us-west-2, use Amazon Route 53 with active-active failover routing, and configure DynamoDB global tables.
Deploy API Gateway and Lambda in us-east-1 with a global Amazon CloudFront distribution pointing to an Amazon S3 static error page as a failover origin.
Deploy API Gateway and Lambda in us-east-1 only, and configure a cold standby environment in us-west-2 using AWS CloudFormation templates triggered by CloudWatch alarms.

questions.explanation: Achieving resilient multi-region serverless applications involves deploying identical serverless stacks (API Gateway + Lambda) across multiple regions, fronting them with latency-based or failover routing via Route 53 or AWS Global Accelerator, and using DynamoDB global tables for database persistence.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Routing traffic globally to a single regional ALB does not provide disaster recovery if the primary region's ALB or compute infrastructure fails.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Pointing to a static error page does not provide application failover or database persistence during an outage.
wrongOptionNotes.D: A cold standby deployed via CloudFormation during an outage results in an unacceptably high RTO for a mission-critical tracking application.

questions.question: A media streaming enterprise is planning a disaster recovery strategy for its video catalog stored in Amazon S3. The company needs to replicate terabytes of existing video assets and ongoing daily uploads from us-east-1 to eu-central-1. The recovery strategy requires an RPO of less than 15 minutes and verification that replication succeeds without data corruption. How should the Solutions Architect fulfill these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) with replication metrics enabled.
Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) enabled, and use S3 Batch Replication for the existing historical video catalog.
Set up an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in us-east-1 to sync data to an S3 bucket in eu-central-1 using scheduled cron jobs.
Write a Python script executed via cron on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses the AWS CLI to sync the S3 buckets every hour.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication combined with S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) provides predictable, SLA-backed replication times (typically within 15 minutes) for petabyte-scale datasets, complemented by S3 Batch Replication for pre-existing objects.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Same-Region Replication does not replicate data across different AWS regions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: AWS Storage Gateway is not optimized for direct petabyte-scale multi-region S3-to-S3 replication compared to native S3 replication features.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Custom scripts lack built-in monitoring, retry logic, and scalable performance for massive data volumes, and an hourly sync violates the 15-minute RPO.

questions.question: An enterprise financial application runs in us-east-1 on Amazon EC2 instances with an Oracle database hosted on Amazon RDS Multi-AZ. The RTO is 1 hour, and the RPO is 5 minutes. The risk management team requests a cross-region disaster recovery plan in us-west-2 that minimizes cost while meeting the RPO and RTO requirements. Which architecture is most appropriate?

options.text: Deploy a cold standby architecture relying on nightly database exports uploaded to Amazon S3 in us-west-2.
Build a multi-site active-active architecture with identical EC2 capacity and synchronous database replication across regions.
Take daily snapshots of the RDS database and EBS volumes, and copy the snapshots to us-west-2.
Implement a pilot light disaster recovery architecture with an Amazon RDS Oracle cross-region read replica in us-west-2 and automated AMIs ready for EC2 deployment via AWS CloudFormation.

questions.explanation: A pilot light disaster recovery pattern maintains a minimal replica of critical core state (such as cross-region database replicas) while keeping compute infrastructure scaled down or unprovisioned until a disaster occurs, balancing cost and recovery speed.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Nightly exports lead to an unacceptable RPO and prolonged RTO during a disaster recovery event.
wrongOptionNotes.B: A multi-site active-active setup exceeds budget and operational complexity when a pilot light architecture satisfies the RPO and RTO at a lower cost.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Daily snapshots result in an RPO of 24 hours, failing the 5-minute RPO requirement.

questions.question: A global gaming company is setting up a disaster recovery architecture for a real-time player statistics platform on AWS. The application must achieve active-active multi-region availability across us-east-1 and ap-southeast-1. The database layer uses Amazon Aurora Global Database. User requests should be routed to the AWS region that provides the lowest network latency. Which service combination provides this routing behavior?

options.text: An Amazon S3 static website hosting bucket configured with cross-region redirection rules.
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) conditional policies based on source IP geolocation.
Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing policies and health checks configured for both regional endpoints.
Amazon CloudFront with failover origin groups and weighted distribution.

questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing uses latency measurements between user networks and AWS regions to serve DNS requests from the region that offers the lowest network latency, optimizing global application performance.

wrongOptionNotes.A: S3 redirection rules do not provide dynamic latency-based routing for active-active backend applications.
wrongOptionNotes.B: IAM policies control access permissions, not network traffic routing.
wrongOptionNotes.D: CloudFront handles content caching and origin failover, but Route 53 latency routing is specifically designed for directing client connections across regions based on network latency.

questions.question: A technology enterprise is reviewing its disaster recovery posture for a core billing application running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer in us-west-1. The business requires an automated multi-region failover mechanism to us-east-2 that operates without manual DNS modifications. Which design satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Deploy a single Network Load Balancer in us-west-1 and configure target groups pointing to EC2 instances in us-east-2.
Configure an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator with endpoint groups in us-west-1 and us-east-2, attaching the respective Application Load Balancers to each endpoint group.
Create a CNAME record in Route 53 pointing the domain name directly to the us-west-1 ALB and update it manually during a failure.
Use Amazon CloudFront with an Amazon S3 bucket as the primary origin and the us-west-1 ALB as the secondary origin.

questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator improves availability and performance by using static anycast IP addresses that route traffic over the AWS global network. It continuously monitors endpoint health and automatically fails over to a secondary region if the primary endpoint fails.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Network Load Balancers cannot target EC2 instances across different AWS regions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Manual updates fail the requirement for automated multi-region failover and introduce high RTO.
wrongOptionNotes.D: An S3 bucket cannot serve as a dynamic compute application origin for a billing application.

questions.question: An insurance company stores policy documents in Amazon S3 in the us-east-1 region. Due to business continuity guidelines, the company must replicate all objects to us-west-2. The security team mandates that replication traffic must remain within the AWS backbone network, and objects must be encrypted at rest using AWS KMS customer managed keys (CMKs). How should this replication be configured?

options.text: Set up an Amazon EC2 instance running rsync in a public subnet to pull data from us-east-1 and push it to us-west-2.
Export the S3 bucket data via a public internet gateway to an external translation server, then upload the data to the destination S3 bucket in us-west-2.

Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) and specify source and destination KMS keys, ensuring the IAM execution role has permissions to decrypt in the source bucket and encrypt in the destination bucket.
Use a scheduled AWS Glue ETL job to read files from the source S3 bucket and write them to the destination S3 bucket.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication securely transfers objects across regions over the AWS global network. When using AWS KMS customer managed keys, S3 CRR can replicate encrypted objects provided the replication IAM role has explicit permissions for both source and destination keys.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Using EC2 instances with rsync introduces single points of failure, scaling challenges, and security risks compared to fully managed S3 CRR.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Routing sensitive policy documents over the public internet violates security best practices and compliance policies.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS Glue ETL jobs introduce unnecessary operational overhead, latency, and cost compared to native S3 Cross-Region Replication.

questions.question: An enterprise is designing a multi-region disaster recovery architecture for a batch-processing workload running on Amazon EC2 instances managed by AWS Batch. The workload processes large datasets stored in Amazon S3. If the primary region (us-east-1) fails, the processing queue and compute jobs must resume in the secondary region (eu-west-1) within 30 minutes. Which architectural pattern should the Solutions Architect implement?

options.text: Replicate input data in S3 using Cross-Region Replication, configure AWS Batch job queues in both regions, and submit batch jobs to the secondary region queue via automation scripts upon primary region failure.
Rely on AWS Shield to automatically migrate AWS Batch job definitions and compute environments across regions during an outage.
Attach a single Amazon EBS volume across both us-east-1 and eu-west-1 instances simultaneously.
Use Amazon SQS FIFO queues with cross-region message duplication enabled to drive AWS Batch.

questions.explanation: For batch processing disaster recovery, input data must be replicated via Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication, and auxiliary compute orchestration resources (such as AWS Batch job definitions and queues) should be pre-configured in the secondary region to enable rapid job resumption.

wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS Shield is a managed DDoS protection service and does not manage cross-region workload migration or AWS Batch orchestration.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Amazon EBS volumes can only be attached to EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone at a time; they cannot span across multiple regions.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Amazon SQS queues are regional constructs and do not support native cross-region message duplication or failover without custom producer/consumer logic.

questions.question: A financial institution is designing a disaster recovery plan for a legacy application running on Microsoft Windows Server on Amazon EC2 instances in us-east-1. The recovery plan requires an automated way to maintain identical EC2 instances and data in us-west-2 with an RPO of 24 hours. Which native AWS service should the Solutions Architect use to meet this requirement efficiently?

options.text: Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan that takes daily Amazon EBS snapshots and AMI images of the EC2 instances in us-east-1 and copies them to us-west-2.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode across both us-east-1 and us-west-2.
Configure Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies to export EC2 instance memory state to us-west-2 every 24 hours.
Write a custom PowerShell script executed via AWS Systems Manager to export system state files to an FTP server in us-west-2.

questions.explanation: AWS Backup provides a centralized, policy-driven service to automate backup scheduling, retention, and cross-region copying of Amazon EC2 AMIs and EBS snapshots, simplifying disaster recovery for EC2-based workloads.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Storage Gateway is for hybrid storage integration, not for mirroring full Windows EC2 instance environments and boot volumes across AWS regions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: S3 lifecycle policies manage object transitions and expiration, not EC2 memory or instance state replication.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Custom PowerShell and FTP setups introduce unnecessary maintenance overhead and security risks compared to managed AWS Backup capabilities.

questions.question: A multinational enterprise wants to enforce a strict security policy requiring that all Amazon S3 buckets created across its hundreds of AWS accounts within an AWS Organization must automatically block all public access by default. The solution must prevent any developer or account administrator from overriding this restriction. Which approach meets these requirements with the least operational overhead?

options.text: Write a centralized AWS CloudFormation Guard policy that runs in a continuous integration pipeline, scanning all infrastructure templates before deployment to ensure S3 public access is blocked.
Implement AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) with explicit deny statements for public S3 APIs and apply them to the root organizational unit.

Configure Amazon S3 Account-Level Block Public Access settings on every existing and future member account using AWS Control Tower proactive controls and AWS Organizations delegated administrator settings.
Deploy an AWS Lambda function triggered by Amazon EventBridge whenever an S3 bucket is created, checking its configuration and applying a public access block configuration via the AWS SDK.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Block Public Access can be configured at the account level. When set, these settings apply to all buckets within the account and cannot be overridden by bucket-level policies or IAM permissions. Utilizing AWS Organizations and account-level settings enforces this governance globally and automatically across all accounts.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Templates scanned in a pipeline cannot prevent manual creation of resources via the AWS Console or AWS CLI directly within member accounts.
wrongOptionNotes.B: While an SCP can block public S3 operations, using S3 Block Public Access at the account level via AWS Account Settings is much cleaner and natively supported without parsing complex API variants in SCP json policies.
wrongOptionNotes.D: This approach is reactive rather than preventative, leaving a short race-condition window where a bucket could briefly be made public before the Lambda execution finishes.

questions.question: An enterprise organization with multiple AWS accounts governed by AWS Organizations wants to ensure that all AWS CloudTrail trails across every member account cannot be deleted or tampered with by any IAM user or role within those accounts, including account administrators. What is the most secure architectural approach?

options.text: Configure individual CloudTrail trails in each member account and apply an explicit IAM deny policy on the AdministratorAccess role to prevent execution of CloudTrail deletion APIs.

Create a centralized CloudTrail trail managed from the organization's management account and store the logs in an S3 bucket in a dedicated logging account with an explicit bucket policy denying delete actions to member accounts.
Enable Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode on the log destination bucket and configure AWS Config to automatically remediate any changes to CloudTrail configurations.
Attach an SCP to all member accounts that explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail to all principals except the organization management account.

questions.explanation: CloudTrail organizational trails are created by the management account (or a delegated administrator account) and replicated across all member accounts. Because the trail is managed from outside the member account, users within member accounts lack the permissions to modify or delete the trail configuration, ensuring logging integrity.

wrongOptionNotes.A: An administrator can easily detach or modify their own IAM policy, rendering this approach ineffective against rogue administrators or compromised admin credentials.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While S3 Object Lock prevents log file deletion, it does not prevent users from stopping or deleting the CloudTrail trail itself, leading to gaps in log collection.
wrongOptionNotes.D: SCPs cannot control actions on resources outside the account where the principal resides for certain cross-account S3 operations, and SCPs cannot target specific internal user IDs easily without complex condition keys.

questions.question: A financial services company is reviewing its IAM architecture. Security auditors discover that an IAM role used by an EC2 application has permissions that are far too broad. The security team wants to restrict the role so that it can only assume another specific role that has the necessary least-privilege permissions, but only when invoked from a specific corporate IP address range. How should this be implemented?

options.text: Configure an Amazon VPC endpoint policy for AWS STS inside the VPC to intercept and drop all assume-role requests originating from unauthorized IP addresses.
Create an SCP on the organization root that restricts sts:AssumeRole calls to the corporate IP range for all roles across the organization.
Modify the target role's Trust Policy to include a Condition block checking aws:SourceIp against the corporate IP range and restricting sts:AssumeRole principals.
Attach an IAM permissions boundary to the calling IAM role that explicitly denies the sts:AssumeRole action if the client IP address is outside the corporate range.

questions.explanation: Role assumption is controlled by the trust policy (resource-based policy) of the role being assumed. You can use condition keys such as aws:SourceIp within the trust policy to ensure that sts:AssumeRole requests can only be executed when initiated from authorized network locations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: VPC endpoint policies for STS can restrict access to specific principals or accounts, but they do not parse incoming source IP headers in a way that filters external client ranges effectively for this workflow.
wrongOptionNotes.B: SCPs cannot evaluate client IP addresses because SCPs evaluate AWS API requests without network context like client IP for most operations.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Permissions boundaries limit the maximum permissions an entity can have, but source IP conditions are typically evaluated in the resource-based policy or trust policy rather than permission boundaries for assume-role context.

questions.question: An enterprise application stores sensitive cryptographic keys in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Compliance requirements mandate that all KMS customer managed keys (CMKs) must be automatically rotated every year, and the security team must have an immutable audit trail proving when keys were rotated. How should this be configured?

options.text: Set the KMS key expiration policy attribute to 365 days using the AWS CLI, forcing KMS to automatically invalidate and recreate the key identifier.
Write a custom AWS Lambda function invoked annually by Amazon EventBridge that generates a new KMS key, re-encrypts all data assets, and updates the application configuration.

Enable automatic key rotation on the KMS keys, which rotates the backing key material every 365 days while preserving the key ID, and monitor key rotation events using Amazon EventBridge and AWS CloudTrail.
Configure an AWS Config custom rule that checks the age of every KMS key and automatically triggers a key replacement workflow when the key reaches 365 days of age.

questions.explanation: AWS KMS provides automatic key rotation for customer managed symmetric encryption keys. When enabled, KMS rotates the backing key material every year. The original key ID remains the same, so applications do not need to be updated, and CloudTrail records the rotation events for compliance audits.

wrongOptionNotes.A: KMS keys do not have an expiration policy attribute that automatically recreates the key identifier; key rotation rotates the backing key material behind the same key ID.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Manual or scripted rotation requires decrypting and re-encrypting all data assets, which is operationally intensive, introduces security risks, and is unnecessary because KMS manages backing key rotation transparently.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS Config is an evaluation and compliance service, not an orchestration or automated remediation tool for cryptographic key replacement.

questions.question: A global enterprise is designing a secure landing zone using AWS Control Tower. Security architects need to ensure that no member account within the organization can launch Amazon EC2 instances without encryption enabled on all attached EBS volumes by default. What is the most effective native mechanism to enforce this rule?

options.text: Enable EBS encryption by default in the EC2 settings of every AWS region across all member accounts.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to listen for EC2 Instance State-change Notification events and terminate any instance found with unencrypted volumes.
Write a Service Control Policy (SCP) that blocks the ec2:CreateVolume API call if the Encrypted parameter is set to false.
Deploy an AWS Config managed rule named ec2-ebs-encryption-enabled and configure automatic remediation using an AWS Systems Manager Automation document.

questions.explanation: Enabling 'EBS encryption by default' in Amazon EC2 settings ensures that all new EBS volumes and volumes created from snapshots are automatically encrypted without requiring explicit configuration in every API request or CloudFormation template. This operates as a preventative safeguard.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Terminating instances reactively is disruptive to production workloads and violates high-availability design best practices.
wrongOptionNotes.C: SCPs cannot evaluate complex conditional logic like checking the internal attributes of a volume creation payload unless structured through specific condition keys, and EBS encryption by default is a cleaner native account-level setting.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Remediating after an instance is already launched leaves a window of vulnerability where unencrypted volumes exist, and Systems Manager remediation can fail if instance profiles lack permissions.

questions.question: An internal application running on Amazon EC2 instances needs to retrieve sensitive database credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
