wrongOptionNotes.B: Increasing deregistration delay prolongs the time the ALB waits before closing connections to unhealthy or terminating instances, which would worsen latency during an outage.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While NLB is high performance, the ALB natively supports cross-zone load balancing, which resolves uneven distribution without needing to change load balancer types.

questions.question: A healthcare enterprise stores compliance audit logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Auditors require that any log object older than 90 days must be transitioned to a cheaper storage tier, and all log objects must be permanently deleted after exactly 7 years (2,555 days) to comply with data minimization laws. Furthermore, objects must not be transitioned to Glacier Flexible Retrieval if they have been accessed within the last 30 days. Which feature should be configured?

options.text: An AWS Lambda function triggered by S3 Event Notifications that parses bucket inventory files and deletes objects older than 2,555 days.
Amazon S3 Batch Operations scheduled via cron jobs to execute daily object deletion and tagging scripts.
Configuring S3 Object Lock retention mode with a permanent legal hold on all objects.
An Amazon S3 Lifecycle configuration featuring transition rules for 90 days, intelligent tiering overrides, and expiration rules set to 2,555 days.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Lifecycle configurations provide native, automated management of object lifecycles. Administrators can define rules to transition objects to cost-effective storage classes after a set number of days and automatically expire objects when they reach their mandatory retention ceiling.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Using custom Lambda functions to manage object lifecycles introduces unnecessary operational complexity, maintenance overhead, and potential execution failures compared to native S3 Lifecycle rules.
wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 Batch Operations are designed for one-time or episodic large-scale batch processing tasks, not as an ongoing lifecycle replacement for automated age-based transitions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Legal holds prevent deletion indefinitely until explicitly removed, which directly contradicts the compliance requirement to permanently delete objects after 7 years.

questions.question: A financial services firm runs a core banking application on Amazon EC2 instances inside a private subnet. The application instances require access to an external third-party credit-scoring API over the public internet. Due to strict security mandates, the third-party API provider requires all inbound requests from the firm to originate from a single, static, elastic public IP address. Which architectural design fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Route outbound traffic from the private subnet through a NAT Gateway associated with a static Elastic IP address.
Attach an Elastic IP address directly to each EC2 application instance inside the private subnet.
Configure an Application Load Balancer in the private subnet with a static IP address provided by AWS Global Accelerator.
Deploy an Internet Gateway directly inside the private subnet and associate an Elastic IP address with the route table.

questions.explanation: To present a static, predictable public IP address for outbound traffic originating from private EC2 instances, architects deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet and associate an Elastic IP address with it. Private subnet route tables then direct outbound internet traffic through this NAT Gateway.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Instances in private subnets cannot have public or Elastic IP addresses attached directly to them because they lack a direct route to an Internet Gateway.
wrongOptionNotes.C: An Application Load Balancer in a private subnet cannot route traffic to the internet without a NAT Gateway or NAT instance, regardless of AWS Global Accelerator.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Internet Gateways can only be attached to VPCs, not directly to subnets or route tables, and attaching one to a private subnet turns it into a public subnet.

questions.question: An e-commerce company operates a high-traffic web application deployed across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. The backend database runs on Amazon RDS MySQL in a Multi-AZ deployment. During a routine game-day disaster drill, the primary database instance is forcibly rebooted. Although the database fails over successfully within 60 seconds, the web application experiences cascading failures and becomes entirely unresponsive for over 15 minutes because connection pools on the EC2 instances remain exhausted. What architectural remediation should be implemented?

options.text: Migrate the RDS database to a Single-AZ deployment with automated read replicas in every Availability Zone.
Implement robust connection retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter in the application code, and configure appropriate connection pool timeouts.
Increase the Application Load Balancer idle timeout from 60 seconds to 600 seconds.
Configure AWS WAF to block all incoming database connection requests during a failover event.

questions.explanation: When databases undergo failover, transient connection drops can cause application connection pools to become saturated with failing threads. Implementing exponential backoff, jitter, and proper connection timeouts prevents application servers from overwhelming recovering databases and avoids cascading failures.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Moving to a Single-AZ setup removes Multi-AZ high availability protections, increasing downtime risk during infrastructure failures.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Increasing the ALB idle timeout keeps connections open longer, which would exacerbate connection pool exhaustion on the backend instances during a database outage.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS web traffic at Layer 7 and cannot intercept or block database connection attempts made by backend application servers.

questions.question: An enterprise web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application occasionally crashes due to memory leaks, leaving the EC2 instances in a running state but incapable of serving HTTP requests. The default EC2 status checks continue to report the instances as healthy, preventing the Auto Scaling group from replacing them. Which solution should be implemented to ensure unhealthy instances are automatically terminated and replaced?

options.text: Attach an Amazon SNS topic to CloudWatch alarms to send email alerts to operations engineers whenever memory usage exceeds 90%.
Configure a scheduled scaling action to replace all instances in the Auto Scaling group every 4 hours.
Increase the frequency of Amazon CloudWatch detailed monitoring from 5-minute intervals to 1-minute intervals.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) health checks alongside EC2 status checks.

questions.explanation: Default EC2 status checks only verify hypervisor and hardware health. When an application becomes unresponsive due to software errors, integrating Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) health checks ensures that the Auto Scaling group detects target failures and automatically replaces unhealthy instances.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Sending email notifications requires manual intervention to remediate instances, failing the requirement for automated replacement.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Scheduled scaling replaces instances on a rigid timetable rather than reacting to actual health failures, which can cause unnecessary disruption.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Detailed monitoring provides more granular metrics, but standard CloudWatch metrics do not include internal application HTTP response status unless custom metrics are published.

questions.question: A global gaming company stores player profile data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes during tournament finals. The engineering team wants to eliminate manual capacity planning and ensure that the DynamoDB table instantly scales up and down to handle variable workloads without incurring throttling errors or paying for unutilized provisioned capacity. Which capacity mode should be selected?

options.text: Configure the DynamoDB table to use On-Demand capacity mode.
Configure Provisioned capacity mode with AWS Auto Scaling enabled for both read and write capacity targets set to 50% utilization.
Provision maximum possible read and write capacity units upfront to cover the peak potential tournament traffic.
Switch the database backend from DynamoDB to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ autoscaling storage.

questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB On-Demand capacity mode is a flexible billing and capacity option that capable of serving workloads with unpredictable traffic spikes instantly. It eliminates the need to specify read and write throughput ahead of time, scaling automatically with application demand.

wrongOptionNotes.B: While Auto Scaling helps with provisioned mode, it has a ramp-up time for sudden spikes, whereas On-Demand provides instant scaling without capacity management.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Over-provisioning capacity permanently to handle rare spikes is cost-prohibitive and violates efficient cloud architecture cost optimization principles.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Migrating relational databases introduces complex connection pooling and scaling overhead that does not solve DynamoDB-specific workload scaling requirements.

questions.question: An e-commerce platform runs its core transaction service on Amazon EC2 instances inside an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). During a flash sale, CloudWatch metrics indicate that the ALB is returning HTTP 502 Bad Gateway errors, and the Auto Scaling group is aggressively launching new instances, but instances are failing health checks immediately upon registration. What is the most likely root cause and remediation?

options.text: The ALB target group health check path is misconfigured or the application takes longer to initialize than the configured health check grace period, causing the ALB to deregister newly launched instances. Adjust the health check grace period and ensure the health check endpoint returns HTTP 200.
The VPC security groups assigned to the ALB allow inbound traffic on port 443, but the security groups on the EC2 instances block outbound traffic to the database.
The Route 53 latency routing policy is sending traffic to unhealthy AWS regions, causing the ALB to return connection reset errors.
The EC2 instances have exhausted their attached Amazon EBS volume IOPS limits, preventing the web server process from writing logs and crashing the operating system kernel.

questions.explanation: HTTP 502 errors from an Application Load Balancer indicate that the load balancer is unable to receive a valid HTTP response from the registered targets. When new instances fail health checks immediately upon launch, it is often because the application takes longer to start than the default health check grace period or target health check interval. Adjusting the Auto Scaling health check grace period and verifying the target group health check settings resolves this boot-loop behavior.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Security group misconfigurations between the ALB and EC2 instances typically result in HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors rather than immediate target health check failures on registration.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Route 53 operates at the DNS layer and does not generate HTTP 502 errors; HTTP 502 errors are explicitly generated by the ALB when it cannot obtain a valid response from registered targets.
wrongOptionNotes.D: EBS throttling would cause high latency or disk errors, but instances failing immediately upon registration point directly to load balancer health check integration issues rather than IOPS exhaustion.

questions.question: A financial data processing system runs on Amazon EC2 instances distributed across three Availability Zones. The instances process incoming messages pulled from an Amazon SQS queue. A recent outage revealed that when a dependent third-party API service experienced latency spikes, the EC2 instances became overwhelmed, processing failures cascaded, and the SQS queue filled up with poisoned messages that triggered infinite retries. Which architectural modification will best resolve this resilience bottleneck?

options.text: Implement a dead-letter queue (DLQ) on the SQS queue, configure a maximum receive count, and integrate AWS Lambda with exponential backoff and circuit breaker patterns for downstream API calls.
Modify the EC2 instances to use synchronous database transactions for every processed queue message to maintain strict consistency across availability zones.
Migrate the SQS queue to an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream with enhanced fan-out to ensure deterministic ordering and prevent message duplication during spikes.
Increase the maximum concurrency of the Auto Scaling group and scale out the EC2 instances to match the peak message volume in the SQS queue.

questions.explanation: To prevent cascading failures and handle poisoned messages during downstream outages, architectures must implement a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) combined with bounded receive counts. Additionally, applying circuit breaker patterns prevents applications from continually retrying failing downstream dependencies.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Adding synchronous database calls to every message processing loop introduces additional latency and potential locking bottlenecks, reducing overall system resilience.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While Kinesis provides ordering, moving away from SQS does not solve the underlying issue of cascading failures caused by downstream API latency without circuit breakers or proper error handling.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Scaling out EC2 instances blindly when downstream dependencies are slow only increases overall connection pressure on the struggling third-party API, worsening the outage.

questions.question: An enterprise SaaS application uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL database cluster spanning two Availability Zones. During a scheduled maintenance event, the primary database instance failed over to the replica in the secondary AZ. However, the application layer experienced a 15-minute complete outage because the connection pool maintained stale IP addresses of the old primary database. What design change prevents this downtime?

options.text: Replace the Amazon Aurora database with a monolithic Oracle database deployed on a single large EC2 instance with EBS snapshot replication.
Configure the application to connect using the Aurora Reader Endpoint so that read and write operations are automatically load-balanced across both availability zones.
Update the application database connection string to use the Aurora Cluster Endpoint and ensure the application runtime honors short TTLs and implements automatic reconnection logic.
Deploy a Hardware Security Module (HSM) proxy in front of the database cluster to intercept and rewrite database connection handles during failover events.

questions.explanation: Aurora automatically manages failover via the Cluster Endpoint, which points to the current primary database instance. To ensure seamless application failover without long outages, applications must be configured to use the Cluster Endpoint and properly handle DNS updates and stale connection reconnections.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Moving to a single EC2 instance eliminates multi-AZ high availability and increases the blast radius of database failures, contradicting resilience goals.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Aurora Reader Endpoints direct traffic exclusively to read replicas and cannot handle write operations, which would cause transaction failures for write-heavy applications.
wrongOptionNotes.D: HSMs are used for cryptographic key management and encryption, not for managing database connection pooling or handling cluster failover routing.

questions.question: A logistics company operates a tracking application running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The operations team reports intermittent HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors during peak tracking hours. CloudWatch metrics show that EC2 CPU utilization remains below 40%, but the ALB 'TargetResponseTime' metric has spiked significantly. What is the most probable cause?

options.text: The backend application threads are blocked waiting for responses from an external REST API or database locks, causing requests to exceed the ALB idle timeout threshold.
The EC2 instances are experiencing CPU throttling due to burst credit exhaustion on t3 instances, preventing thread scheduling.
The ALB has reached its maximum concurrent connection limit and is dropping incoming TCP SYN packets before they reach target EC2 instances.
The Route 53 health checker has marked the primary region as unhealthy and is routing all client traffic to a secondary static error bucket.

questions.explanation: An HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout means the load balancer timed out waiting for a response from the target instance. When CPU utilization is low but TargetResponseTime is high, it signifies that the application threads are idle, waiting on external I/O operations, database queries, or lock contention.

wrongOptionNotes.B: If CPU throttling or credit exhaustion were occurring, overall CPU utilization metrics would reflect exhaustion or application threads would stall entirely, but low CPU points away from this.
wrongOptionNotes.C: ALBs scale automatically to handle varying request rates. Connection drops due to scaling limits manifest as HTTP 503 Service Unavailable errors, not HTTP 504 Gateway Timeouts.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Route 53 failing over would redirect traffic entirely, whereas intermittent 504 errors during peak hours indicate live target timeout conditions under load.

questions.question: A global media company stores high-value video assets in an Amazon S3 bucket. A rogue script accidentally deleted thousands of objects. Although S3 Versioning is enabled, manual restoration is too slow. The architecture team needs a resilient automated recovery strategy that protects against accidental or malicious deletions while minimizing operational overhead.

options.text: Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode on the S3 bucket with a 30-day retention period, and configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to trigger an AWS Lambda function that restores deleted versions.
Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance mode, implement S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to a secondary locked bucket in another AWS region, and enable MFA Delete on the primary bucket.
Write a daily cron job on an EC2 instance that downloads all bucket contents to local Amazon EBS snapshots and compresses them into Glacier Flexible Retrieval vaults.
Configure S3 Lifecycle policies to transition deleted object marker records to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately upon detection of anomalous object count drops.

questions.explanation: To protect against accidental or malicious deletion of S3 objects while maintaining operational flexibility, architects should use S3 Object Lock in Governance mode (or Compliance mode where strict immutability is required), configure Cross-Region Replication to an isolated bucket, and enable MFA Delete for sensitive operations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Compliance mode prevents any user—including the root account—from deleting objects during the retention period, which breaks legitimate operational deletion workflows and cannot be undone easily.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Custom backup scripts running on EC2 introduce high operational overhead, maintenance burdens, and potential script failures, failing to leverage native S3 data protection features.
wrongOptionNotes.D: S3 Lifecycle policies manage storage tiers and expiration, not automated detection and recovery of malicious deletions or accidental bucket purging.

questions.question: An enterprise web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances within private subnets, backed by an Amazon Aurora database. The security team mandates that all traffic between the EC2 instances and the database must be encrypted in transit and authenticated using IAM database authentication. Which combination of steps should a Solutions Architect implement to satisfy these compliance requirements?

options.text: Enable SSL/TLS on the Aurora database cluster, configure the EC2 IAM role with therds-db:connect permission, and use an authentication token generated by the AWS CLI or SDK when connecting.
Configure security groups to allow traffic only on port 3306, store the database master password in AWS Secrets Manager, and have the application fetch the password at startup.
Attach an IAM policy to the EC2 instances granting full AmazonRDSFullAccess, modify the database subnet group to be public, and enforce SSL via parameter groups.
Install a self-signed SSL certificate on each EC2 instance and configure the Aurora cluster to use Kerberos authentication integrated with AWS Directory Service.

questions.explanation: IAM database authentication allows you to authenticate to Aurora and RDS using AWS IAM credentials and temporary authentication tokens, eliminating the need to manage static database passwords. All connections must use TLS/SSL encryption for security.

wrongOptionNotes.B: This uses password-based authentication instead of IAM database authentication and does not guarantee encryption in transit without explicit TLS configuration.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Granting full RDS access violates least-privilege principles, and making the database subnet public introduces severe security risks.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Kerberos authentication is an alternative mechanism, but IAM database authentication combined with standard TLS tokens is the native AWS-managed approach requested.

questions.question: A financial services company is storing compliance records in an Amazon S3 bucket. To comply with regulatory frameworks, the security team requires that any accidental deletion of objects by rogue administrators or compromised credentials must be prevented. Which configuration provides the strongest protection against data deletion?

options.text: Enable AWS CloudTrail data events for the bucket and set up Amazon EventBridge rules to automatically restore deleted objects using Lambda.
Enable S3 Versioning and apply an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Archive after 0 days.
Configure an S3 Bucket Policy that explicitly denies the s3:DeleteObject action for all IAM users except the security auditor role.
Enable S3 Versioning and apply an S3 Object Lock configuration in Compliance mode with a specified retention period.

questions.explanation: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode is designed for strict regulatory compliance, ensuring that objects cannot be overwritten or deleted by any user, including the account root user, for the duration of the retention period.

wrongOptionNotes.A: This is a reactive remediation approach with a time gap during which data is missing, rather than a preventive control.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Lifecycle policies do not prevent object deletion or overwriting; they only transition storage classes or expire objects.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Bucket policies can be modified or deleted by someone with administrative permissions on the bucket, whereas S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode cannot be overridden even by the root account.

questions.question: An organization is deploying multiple microservices across several AWS accounts managed through AWS Organizations. The security team needs to enforce a mandatory guardrail ensuring that no developer can create an Amazon S3 bucket without server-side encryption enabled by default. Where should this policy be applied?

options.text: Deploy an AWS CloudTrail trail in each account and use Amazon EventBridge to trigger an AWS Lambda function that deletes unencrypted buckets.
Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the organization root or organizational unit (OU) level that denies s3:CreateBucket if encryption headers are absent.
Create an IAM policy and attach it to every developer's IAM user profile across all accounts in the AWS organization.
Configure AWS Trusted Advisor rules in the management account to automatically remediate unencrypted S3 buckets upon creation.

questions.explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) are JSON policies used to manage permissions in an organization, serving as guardrails to set maximum available permissions for member accounts in AWS Organizations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Reactive deletion after creation can lead to data loss or race conditions; preventive controls via SCPs are architecturally superior.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Managing individual IAM policies across numerous accounts is operationally inefficient and prone to drift; SCPs provide centralized governance.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations and some auto-remediation, but it is not a preventive enforcement mechanism like an SCP.

questions.question: A multinational corporation requires that all Amazon EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances across the entire AWS infrastructure must be encrypted automatically upon creation. The Solutions Architect needs a native AWS feature to enforce this requirement with minimal operational overhead.

options.text: Write a custom AWS Config rule that triggers an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to encrypt unencrypted volumes daily.
Implement an Amazon EventBridge rule listening for EC2 volume creation events and invoke a Lambda function to detach and encrypt the volume.
Enable EBS encryption by default in all AWS Regions across all accounts within the organization using AWS Organizations and AWS KMS.
Configure an IAM policy denying the ec2:CreateVolume action unless the request specifies an encryption key explicitly.

questions.explanation: Amazon EBS encryption by default is a regional setting that automatically encrypts new EBS volumes and snapshots with minimal effort, satisfying security compliance baselines instantly.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS Config is detective, and running periodic batch encryption leaves a window of vulnerability where newly created volumes remain unencrypted.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Detaching and modifying volumes post-creation causes application downtime and race conditions, whereas encryption by default prevents unencrypted creation natively.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While condition keys can enforce encryption parameters, enabling EBS encryption by default is the native, zero-maintenance setting designed specifically for this requirement.

questions.question: An internal web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and requires access to sensitive API keys stored in AWS Secrets Manager. To adhere to security best practices, the EC2 instances must not store long-term credentials. How should the Solutions Architect design the authentication and access mechanism?

options.text: Attach an IAM role with permissions to retrieve the specific secret to the EC2 instances, and have the application use the AWS SDK to fetch the secret dynamically.
Configure the security groups of the EC2 instances to trust the Secrets Manager service endpoint without requiring authentication.
Store the database and API credentials in an encrypted configuration file bundled directly inside the application deployment package.
Create an IAM user for each EC2 instance, generate long-term access keys, and store them in environment variables on the instances.

questions.explanation: EC2 instance profiles assign IAM roles to virtual servers, supplying temporary security credentials via the instance metadata service. This eliminates the need to embed credentials in application code.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Security groups control network traffic, not identity or authentication.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Bundling credentials inside deployment artifacts increases exposure risk and makes rotation difficult.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Using IAM users and long-term access keys on EC2 instances violates AWS security best practices for compute resources.

questions.question: A healthcare analytics platform stores sensitive patient records in Amazon S3. The security team requires that all data must be encrypted at rest using a customer-managed AWS KMS key. Furthermore, the security team must be able to independently audit key usage and have the ability to instantly revoke access to the data by disabling the key. Which configuration should be implemented?

options.text: Encrypt all files client-side using a static password shared securely among data scientists via an internal wiki.
Configure S3 bucket default encryption using AWS KMS (SSE-KMS) with a customer managed key, and monitor access via AWS CloudTrail.
Use Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) and attach a resource-based policy denying access when compliance officers are offline.
Store the data in unencrypted S3 buckets and rely entirely on VPC endpoint policies to restrict who can read the data.

questions.explanation: Server-Side Encryption with Customer Managed Keys (SSE-KMS) provides granular control over encryption keys, comprehensive logging of cryptographic operations via CloudTrail, and instant revocation capabilities.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Client-side encryption with shared static passwords is insecure, prone to leakage, and lacks centralized auditing.
wrongOptionNotes.C: SSE-S3 uses AWS-managed keys where customers cannot manage key rotation schedules or access keys directly.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Relying solely on network controls leaves data unencrypted at rest, failing encryption compliance requirements.

questions.question: An external security audit reveals that several Amazon S3 buckets containing proprietary data are publicly accessible via ACLs and bucket policies. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) demands an immediate, account-wide mechanism to block public access across all current and future S3 buckets, regardless of individual bucket settings.

options.text: Modify the default VPC security groups associated with the account to drop all inbound traffic originating from public IP addresses.
Enable Amazon S3 Block Public Access at the AWS account level.
Delete all S3 buckets containing proprietary data and recreate them with default encryption enabled.
Manually inspect every S3 bucket in the account and remove public read permissions from each individual bucket policy and ACL.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Block Public Access provides settings at the bucket, account, or AWS Organization level to easily manage public access to S3 resources, overriding any conflicting permissions.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Security groups apply to EC2 instances and ENIs, not to Amazon S3 buckets.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Deleting buckets causes permanent data loss and does not inherently fix public access permissions unless Block Public Access is used.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Manual inspection is time-consuming, prone to human error, and fails to prevent future buckets from being created with public access.

questions.question: A financial services organization needs to establish secure, private connectivity between its on-premises data center and an Amazon VPC hosting sensitive workloads. The connection must not traverse the public internet, must support high throughput, and must be encrypted. Which architecture meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon VPC peering connection between the on-premises data center router and the AWS VPC virtual private gateway.
Set up an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the public internet using standard public routing and static IP addresses.
Deploy a fleet of proxy EC2 instances in public subnets with Elastic IPs and route all on-premises traffic through them over HTTPS.
Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection combined with an IPsec VPN tunnel running over the Direct Connect link for encryption in transit.

questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private connection from an on-premises network to AWS. Pairing it with an AWS VPN delivers both private routing and encrypted tunnels.

wrongOptionNotes.A: VPC peering connects AWS VPCs together, not an on-premises data center to an AWS VPC.
wrongOptionNotes.B: A standard Site-to-Site VPN traverses the public internet, which violates the requirement to avoid public internet routing.
wrongOptionNotes.C: This approach routes traffic over the public internet through proxy instances, introducing operational overhead and single points of failure.

questions.question: An e-commerce enterprise uses AWS Lambda functions to process payment transactions. The Lambda functions need to access a secure database residing in a private VPC subnet. To maintain strict security, the Lambda functions must operate inside the VPC, and outbound traffic to external payment gateways must be strictly controlled and inspected. How should the architecture be designed?

options.text: Configure the Lambda functions outside the VPC and open inbound database security group rules to allow any public IP address.
Attach an Internet Gateway directly to the private subnet route tables where the Lambda functions execute.
Deploy the Lambda functions in public subnets and assign public IP addresses so they can communicate with the database and payment gateways directly.
Deploy the Lambda functions inside private subnets of the VPC, and route outbound internet traffic through a centralized NAT Gateway attached to a transit network or firewall.

questions.explanation: Configuring AWS Lambda to run within a VPC allows secure access to internal resources, while routing egress traffic through NAT gateways and firewalls enforces outbound security controls.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Opening database ports to public IP addresses is a critical security vulnerability.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Private subnets by definition do not have direct routes to an Internet Gateway; doing so turns them into public subnets.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Placing compute workloads in public subnets unnecessarily exposes them to internet threats and violates security baselines.

questions.question: A global company has multiple AWS accounts. The security team needs a centralized solution to continuously monitor security posture, detect misconfigurations (such as open security groups or unencrypted S3 buckets), and automate remediation workflows across all accounts. Which AWS service combination fulfills this requirement?

options.text: Configure AWS IAM Access Analyzer in a single member account and disable AWS CloudTrail in all other accounts to save costs.
Install individual open-source network scanners on EC2 instances in each AWS account and aggregate the logs into an Amazon S3 bucket.
Enable Amazon CloudWatch alarms on every EC2 instance to send emails to the security team whenever an API call fails.
Use AWS Organizations to designate a delegated administrator for AWS Security Hub and Amazon GuardDuty, integrated with AWS Systems Manager Automation for remediation.

questions.explanation: AWS Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of your security state across AWS accounts and checks your environment against security industry standards and best practices.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Disabling CloudTrail severely impairs auditing capabilities and security visibility.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Managing third-party scanners across multiple accounts introduces significant operational overhead and lacks native AWS integration.
wrongOptionNotes.C: CloudWatch alarms are unsuited for posture management and security configuration auditing across multi-account structures.

questions.question: A financial technology startup is launching an application that processes credit card data, requiring compliance with PCI-DSS standards. The architecture includes an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and backend EC2 instances. The security auditor requests proof that all incoming client connections negotiate strong cipher suites and disable outdated protocols such as TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1. How should the Solutions Architect configure the ALB?

options.text: Attach a self-signed certificate to the ALB listener and rely on backend EC2 instances to terminate TLS using custom Apache configurations.
Configure the ALB HTTPS listener with a modern security policy (such as ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06) that enforces TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
Modify the default VPC network ACLs to block packets containing TLS 1.0 handshake headers.
Use HTTP on the ALB listener and route unencrypted traffic to private EC2 instances where encryption is handled internally.

questions.explanation: AWS Application Load Balancers support predefined security policies that control SSL/TLS negotiation. Using modern policies ensures compliance by disallowing deprecated protocols and weak ciphers.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Self-signed certificates fail browser trust validations, and offloading TLS termination improperly leaves the ALB exposed to weak cipher negotiations.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Network ACLs operate at layer 3 and 4 (IP and TCP/UDP) and cannot inspect or filter application-layer TLS handshake versions.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Leaving client-to-ALB traffic unencrypted violates encryption-in-transit compliance requirements for financial data.

questions.question: An enterprise requires that all AWS API activity across its multi-account environment be permanently logged, immutable, and protected from deletion or tampering, even by account administrators. The security team plans to use AWS CloudTrail. Which configuration satisfies the immutability and tamper-resistance requirements?

options.text: Rely on default CloudTrail 90-day event history combined with weekly manual exports to a local workstation.
Set up a standard CloudTrail trail in each member account pointing to a local S3 bucket, and restrict bucket access using standard IAM policies.
Configure an organization trail writing to a centralized S3 bucket that has S3 Object Lock enabled in Compliance mode.
Enable CloudTrail and stream all logs directly to Amazon CloudWatch Logs with an indefinite retention period and no encryption.

questions.explanation: To ensure log integrity and prevent tampering, CloudTrail logs should be written to an S3 bucket configured with S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode, ensuring write-once-read-many (WORM) storage.

wrongOptionNotes.A: The 90-day event history is insufficient for long-term compliance auditing, and manual exports are prone to failure and tampering.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Standard IAM policies can be modified by account administrators, failing to provide protection against administrative tampering.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While CloudWatch Logs provides retention settings, CloudTrail logs stored in S3 with Object Lock provide stronger compliance guarantees for forensic immutability.

questions.question: A software development company hosts its source code repositories on Amazon EC2 instances. Due to intellectual property policies, developers must connect to these instances for remote management without opening inbound SSH ports (port 22) on the security groups or deploying a bastion host. Which AWS service provides a secure mechanism for this requirement?

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in public subnets to route incoming SSH traffic to the private EC2 instances.
Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to securely connect to the EC2 instances through managed SSM agents without inbound ports.
Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection and attach Elastic IPs directly to every developer workstation.
Open SSH port 22 in the security group but restrict the source IP range to the corporate office public IP address.

questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure and auditable node management without the need to open inbound ports, maintain bastion hosts, or manage SSH keys.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Application Load Balancers operate at layers 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and cannot proxy raw TCP protocols like SSH (port 22).
wrongOptionNotes.C: Attaching public IPs to developer workstations introduces significant management and security complexity compared to native AWS tooling.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While IP restriction improves security, leaving port 22 open still presents an attack surface that Session Manager successfully eliminates.

questions.question: An online media company is designing a web application where users upload user-generated profile pictures directly to an Amazon S3 bucket. Security policies dictate that the web application backend must generate a secure, time-limited URL allowing the client browser to upload directly to S3 without exposing AWS credentials to the end user. Which feature should the Solutions Architect use?

options.text: Configure the S3 bucket to allow anonymous write access via public bucket ACLs.
Store long-term AWS IAM access keys in client-side JavaScript code so the browser can authenticate directly with Amazon S3.
Generate Amazon S3 pre-signed URLs using the AWS SDK on the backend application server.
Create an IAM user for every web application visitor and assign them temporary inline policies.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 pre-signed URLs enable developers to grant temporary access to objects and operations by signing the request with the credentials of the AWS IAM user or role that generated the URL.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Allowing anonymous write access enables anyone on the internet to upload arbitrary files, creating severe security and cost risks.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Embedding long-term AWS credentials in client-side code is a critical security vulnerability that exposes the AWS account to compromise.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Creating individual IAM users for web visitors violates IAM scaling limits and operational best practices.

questions.question: A financial firm runs a multi-tier application inside an AWS VPC. Compliance standards require that all network traffic traversing between different private subnets within the same VPC must be inspected and filtered based on fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) and Layer 7 protocols. Which native AWS service should the Solutions Architect implement?

options.text: Attach an AWS WAF web ACL directly to the route tables of the private subnets.
Configure standard security groups on the Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) of the instances in each private subnet.
Deploy AWS Network Firewall in dedicated inspection subnets and route inter-subnet traffic through firewall endpoints.
Implement Amazon VPC Network ACLs with custom rules blocking outbound traffic to unauthorized IP addresses.

questions.explanation: AWS Network Firewall makes it easy to deploy essential protections for all of your Amazon VPCs, supporting granular controls like domain filtering to meet strict security and compliance requirements.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS WAF protects web applications at layer 7 (HTTP/General web traffic) on ALBs, API Gateways, or CloudFront, and cannot be attached to VPC route tables for internal subnet traffic.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Security groups operate at layers 3 and 4 (IP protocols, ports) and cannot filter based on Layer 7 FQDNs.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Network ACLs are stateless subnet-level firewalls that operate on IPs and ports, lacking Layer 7 FQDN inspection capabilities.

questions.question: A global e-commerce platform runs its catalog service on Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Traffic spikes unpredictably during flash sales, causing high latency due to database connection exhaustion and CPU saturation on the backend instances. The business requires a highly scalable architecture that minimizes cost during idle periods while strictly preventing dropped requests during traffic surges.

options.text: Migrate the stateful business logic to AWS Lambda and configure Amazon API Gateway in front of it to handle asynchronous queuing and auto-scaling per request.
Deploy a single monolithic instance of maximum size in an AWS Region and scale vertically by modifying instance types during traffic surges.
Provision a heavily over-provisioned cluster of bare-metal EC2 instances using manual capacity planning to ensure peak capacity is always immediately available.
Use an Amazon CloudFront distribution with a static cache TTL of 24 hours to serve all dynamic product catalog queries.

questions.explanation: Serverless architectures using AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway offer ideal cost-performance tradeoffs for spiky, unpredictable workloads. They eliminate idle compute costs by scaling down to zero while providing instantaneous scaling capabilities that prevent request drops during sudden flash sales.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Vertical scaling of EC2 instances requires downtime or interruption, fails to provide instantaneous elasticity, and creates a single point of failure.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Over-provisioning manual instances completely violates cost optimization principles during idle periods, resulting in exorbitant waste.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Dynamic catalog queries require real-time inventory and pricing data; caching everything for 24 hours results in stale data and failed user checkouts.

questions.question: An enterprise analytics team processes 10 TB of raw log files daily stored in Amazon S3 Standard. The files are queried once a week using Amazon Athena, but compliance mandates that all files must be retained for exactly 3 years. The Chief Financial Officer demands a significant reduction in monthly storage costs without violating durability or compliance rules.

options.text: Delete the S3 bucket every week after running the Athena queries and re-upload the logs from on-premises tapes.
Transition the S3 objects automatically via lifecycle policies to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) immediately after ingestion.
Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Archive after 30 days and delete them after 3 years.
Move all objects to Amazon EBS provisioned IOPS (io2) volumes attached to an idle EC2 instance for local querying.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies allow automated transitions of data across storage tiers. For infrequently accessed compliance archives, moving objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive drastically reduces storage costs while maintaining high durability and availability for scheduled weekly queries.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Re-uploading 10 TB weekly incurs massive data transfer out/in costs and operational overhead, violating compliance retention integrity.
wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 Standard-IA has a minimum billable storage duration of 30 days and retrieval fees. For data queried only once a week with a 3-year retention, S3 Glacier Flexible Archive or S3 Glacier Deep Archive is far more cost-effective.
wrongOptionNotes.D: EBS provisioned IOPS is orders of magnitude more expensive than S3 storage tiers and introduces significant management complexity for 10 TB of data.

questions.question: A digital media agency stores 500 TB of high-resolution video assets in Amazon S3. Access patterns show that 80 percent of the assets are accessed heavily for the first 30 days, rarely accessed between 30 and 90 days, and almost never accessed after 90 days, though retrieval must remain available within minutes if requested. The architecture must minimize storage expenditure.

options.text: Immediately move all newly uploaded video assets to S3 Glacier Deep Archive upon upload.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and S3 Glacier Flexible Archive after 90 days.
Keep all objects in Amazon S3 Standard and use CloudFront edge caching exclusively.
Write a custom cron job on EC2 to download, compress, and re-upload files to local instance storage.

questions.explanation: Utilizing S3 Lifecycle policies with tiered transitions (S3 Standard -> S3 Standard-IA -> S3 Glacier Flexible Archive) aligns storage costs directly with the declining lifecycle access frequency of media assets, achieving maximum savings without sacrificing compliance or retrieval SLAs.

wrongOptionNotes.A: S3 Glacier Deep Archive requires hours for retrieval, which fails the requirement that assets must be available within minutes during the first 90 days.
wrongOptionNotes.C: CloudFront edge caching does not reduce S3 storage pricing for rarely accessed origin files stored in S3 Standard, leading to unnecessarily high monthly storage bills.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Building custom scripts to manage 500 TB of video assets introduces severe operational risk, maintenance overhead, and lacks native S3 durability.

questions.question: A financial data processing system runs background analytics jobs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group. The jobs are fault-tolerant, checkpoint their progress to Amazon S3, and can be interrupted and resumed at any time without data corruption. The engineering manager requires the most cost-effective compute strategy possible.

options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances backed by multiple instance types across multiple Availability Zones.
Run all workloads exclusively on On-Demand instances to guarantee zero interruption risk.
Purchase 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for 100 percent of the maximum anticipated peak capacity.
Deploy dedicated hosts for all batch processing jobs to satisfy strict tenant isolation mandates.

questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances provide spare compute capacity at discounts of up to 90%. For fault-tolerant batch workloads that can handle interruptions and persist state externally, Spot Instances represent the ultimate cost-optimization strategy.

wrongOptionNotes.B: On-Demand pricing is the most expensive compute option and is unnecessary for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch jobs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Reserved Instances provide discounts for steady-state workloads, but for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch jobs, Spot Instances offer significantly greater savings.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Dedicated Hosts are the most costly EC2 pricing model and are only required for specific licensing compliance, not standard batch analytics.

questions.question: An enterprise web application is backed by an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-AZ database cluster. Read traffic has increased by 400 percent, primarily driven by reporting queries that do not require real-time transactional consistency. The primary database instance is showing high CPU utilization, and stakeholders have set a strict budget limit, prohibiting any increase in primary instance sizing.

options.text: Scale up the primary database instance to the next larger instance family immediately.
Migrate the entire database to a fleet of unmanaged EC2 instances running PostgreSQL.
Disable Multi-AZ deployment to free up system resources on the primary instance.
Add Amazon Aurora Replicas in different Availability Zones and route read-only reporting queries to the reader endpoint.

questions.explanation: Aurora Replicas share the same underlying storage as the primary instance, making them a cost-effective way to scale read capacity. Routing read traffic to Aurora replicas relieves CPU pressure on the primary instance without requiring expensive vertical scaling.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Scaling up the primary instance violates the strict budget constraint and does not isolate analytical reporting queries from transactional traffic.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Moving to unmanaged EC2 increases operational overhead and maintenance burden without solving the core scaling problem efficiently.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Disabling Multi-AZ destroys high availability and creates an unacceptable single point of failure for an enterprise database.

questions.question: A multinational corporation runs a nightly reporting job that queries an Amazon Redshift data warehouse cluster. The cluster is utilized for only 4 hours every night but currently runs 24/7, incurring substantial idle hourly charges. The finance department requires a solution to drastically cut Redshift expenditure without rewriting data pipelines.

options.text: Pause the Amazon Redshift cluster immediately after the nightly job completes and resume it automatically before the next scheduled run.
Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances for the cluster while keeping it running 24/7.
Delete the Redshift cluster every morning and recreate it using automated AWS CloudFormation templates every evening.
Migrate all data warehouse tables to Amazon DynamoDB on-demand tables.

questions.explanation: For intermittent data warehousing workloads, pausing the Amazon Redshift cluster eliminates compute costs during idle periods. Users only pay for active compute hours and baseline storage, yielding maximum cost savings for batch reporting schedules.

wrongOptionNotes.B: While reserved instances offer discounts, running a cluster 24/7 when it is only needed 4 hours a day still results in paying for 20 hours of completely wasted compute time.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Deleting and recreating clusters involves complex snapshot restorations, schema rebuilding, and risks data loss or extended downtime compared to native pausing.
wrongOptionNotes.D: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store unsuited for complex analytical SQL joins and massive aggregation queries typical of data warehouses.

questions.question: An API-driven SaaS application experiences predictable diurnal traffic patterns: high request volumes during business hours (9 AM to 5 PM) and near-zero traffic overnight. The backend runs on AWS Lambda integrated with Amazon DynamoDB. The finance team wants to optimize DynamoDB provisioned costs without risking throttled requests during peak morning hours.

options.text: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS MySQL with provisioned IOPS storage.
Configure DynamoDB Auto Scaling on the write and read capacity units with target utilization set to 70 percent, paired with scheduled scaling policies for predictable daily ramps.
Switch DynamoDB tables permanently to On-Demand capacity mode.
Provision maximum read and write capacity units statically to cover peak load 24 hours a day.

questions.explanation: DynamoDB Auto Scaling combined with scheduled scaling provides optimal cost efficiency for predictable diurnal workloads. It prevents over-provisioning during off-peak hours while automatically ensuring sufficient capacity during high-traffic windows.

wrongOptionNotes.A: RDS MySQL requires managing server instances and does not scale automatically like DynamoDB, increasing administrative overhead and costs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While On-Demand handles unpredictable spikes well, for highly predictable diurnal workloads, provisioned capacity with Auto Scaling is significantly more cost-effective.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Statically provisioning peak capacity 24/7 results in paying for massive amounts of unused throughput during overnight hours.

questions.question: A web startup hosts its static frontend assets and media files on Amazon S3 behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The finance director notices that data transfer out (DTO) costs from CloudFront to end-users are consuming a major portion of the operational budget. The architecture needs optimization to lower outbound data costs.

options.text: Move all static assets to Amazon EBS volumes attached to a single EC2 instance acting as a web server.
Enable CloudFront compression, configure appropriate cache behaviors with optimized caching headers, and utilize Price Class 100 or 200 based on user geographic distribution.
Bypass CloudFront and serve all static assets directly from the Amazon S3 bucket public URL.
Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket serving the website users.

questions.explanation: Optimizing CloudFront configurations through asset compression, maximizing cache hit ratios, and selecting appropriate geographic price classes reduces the volume of data transferred and leverages lower-cost edge regions, directly lowering DTO expenses.

wrongOptionNotes.A: This introduces a single point of failure, limits throughput bandwidth, and increases management overhead compared to serverless content delivery.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Serving files directly from S3 incurs higher S3 data transfer out costs and lacks edge caching benefits, increasing overall latency and bandwidth charges.
wrongOptionNotes.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes ingestion uploads into AWS edge locations, not outbound content delivery to end-users, and adds extra cost.

questions.question: An analytics firm runs a large Apache Spark data processing cluster on Amazon EMR. The jobs run for 6 hours every day. The company is locked into a strict annual IT budget and needs to ensure that EMR compute expenditures are minimized without risking cluster instability.

options.text: Permanently terminate the EMR cluster after every job and rebuild all Spark binaries from scratch daily.
Use 100 percent On-Demand instances for the core, task, and master nodes.
Configure the EMR cluster with On-Demand master and core nodes for stability, and utilize Spot instances for the task nodes to handle heavy data processing cheaply.
Run the entire EMR cluster on a single oversized EC2 instance to eliminate cluster communication overhead.

questions.explanation: EMR instance fleet and instance group configurations allow blending On-Demand and Spot instances. Keeping master and core nodes on On-Demand guarantees cluster stability, while using Spot instances for task nodes provides substantial cost savings.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Rebuilding cluster environments daily adds unnecessary bootstrap time, operational complexity, and potential points of failure.
wrongOptionNotes.B: 100 percent On-Demand instances represent the highest cost configuration for EMR clusters and violate budget constraints.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Running distributed big data workloads on a single instance defeats the purpose of EMR and causes out-of-memory errors and job failures.

questions.question: A financial institution runs a core banking application on Amazon EC2 instances inside a private VPC. The instances frequently download large software patches and reference datasets from external public repositories over the internet. Network egress costs are scaling rapidly, prompting management to find a more cost-effective and secure routing architecture.

options.text: Attach public IP addresses directly to all internal EC2 instances so they can download patches directly over Internet Gateways.
Route all internet-bound traffic through a costly third-party virtual firewall appliance deployed in a public subnet.
Provision AWS VPC endpoints (Gateway type for Amazon S3 and Interface type for other services) and set up AWS NAT Gateways.
Deploy Amazon VPC Gateway Endpoints for Amazon S3 and configure Interface VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for other supported AWS services.

questions.explanation: AWS VPC Endpoints (Gateway and Interface) keep traffic within the Amazon private network. This avoids internet egress fees, eliminates NAT Gateway hourly and data processing charges, and enhances security by avoiding public internet exposure.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Attaching public IPs to internal application instances in private subnets violates core enterprise security standards and exposes them to inbound internet threats.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Deploying third-party firewalls adds unnecessary licensing costs and complexity for simply downloading routine patches.
wrongOptionNotes.C: NAT Gateways charge hourly fees plus data processing fees. If traffic is going to AWS services, Gateway VPC endpoints are completely free of hourly and data processing charges.

questions.question: A gaming company hosts a backend matchmaking service on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. The service experiences high traffic during weekends and weekday evenings, but remains mostly idle during early morning hours. The financial controller wants to reduce Fargate compute spend during quiet hours without manual intervention.

options.text: Manually update the ECS task count to zero every night using custom bash scripts.
Migrate all Fargate tasks to fixed-size Amazon EC2 instances running 24/7.
Set the Fargate CPU and memory configuration to the maximum possible limits to ensure high performance at all times.
Configure Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking scaling policies combined with AWS Application Auto Scaling scheduled actions.

questions.explanation: Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling combined with scheduled actions provides automated capacity management, scaling down container tasks during predictable low-traffic windows to save on compute costs without manual intervention.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Manual scripts are prone to human error, lack resilience, and do not constitute an automated enterprise architecture.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Using fixed-size EC2 instances 24/7 eliminates elasticity and increases baseline cost during idle periods.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Maximum resource allocation for idle workloads results in severe financial waste and violates cost optimization guidelines.

questions.question: An online education platform stores 200 TB of course video files in Amazon S3 Standard. The videos are streamed globally by students. Over the last six months, 90 percent of the videos have not been viewed even once. The platform engineering team is tasked with reducing S3 storage expenditures immediately.

options.text: Keep all objects in S3 Standard and enable Cross-Region Replication to three additional AWS Regions.
Migrate the video files to Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD (gp3) volumes.
Write a lifecycle policy to transition objects that have not been accessed for 90 days to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Archive or S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Delete all unviewed video files permanently from the S3 bucket to save storage.

questions.explanation: Identifying cold data and applying S3 Lifecycle transition rules to move unaccessed objects to S3 Glacier storage classes provides massive cost savings for large-scale object repositories without requiring application rewrites.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Replicating cold data across multiple regions multiplies storage costs by four, drastically worsening the financial expenditure.
wrongOptionNotes.B: EBS storage is significantly more expensive per gigabyte than S3 and is attached to EC2 instances, making it completely unsuitable for 200 TB of object storage.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Deleting course content permanently breaks the catalog offerings and hurts the business, whereas cold storage tiers allow retention at low cost.

questions.question: A retail enterprise runs a mission-critical order processing application on Amazon EC2 instances. The system requires steady-state capacity 24/7 throughout the year, but experiences predictable surges during Black Friday. The finance department mandates finding the most cost-effective purchasing option for the baseline steady-state capacity.

options.text: Rely entirely on On-Demand instances year-round to maintain maximum flexibility.
Deploy Dedicated Hosts for all production workloads to maximize hardware control.
Purchase Compute Savings Plans or 3-year Standard Reserved Instances for the steady-state baseline capacity.
Use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances for 100 percent of the mission-critical order processing baseline.

questions.explanation: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances provide significant financial discounts for predictable, steady-state compute workloads by committing to consistent usage over 1-year or 3-year terms, forming the cornerstone of AWS cost optimization.

wrongOptionNotes.A: On-Demand pricing is the most expensive model and wastes budget on predictable, year-round steady-state workloads.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Dedicated Hosts are billed at a premium and are unnecessary unless mandated by strict software licensing rules tied to physical sockets or cores.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Spot instances can be reclaimed with a 2-minute warning, making them unsuitable for mission-critical steady-state database or order processing baselines where availability is paramount.

questions.question: A digital marketing firm operates a high-volume web crawler running on hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances. The jobs are containerized, run for 2 to 4 hours, and can fail or be stopped at any moment without impacting business operations. Management wants to optimize compute costs as aggressively as possible.

options.text: Run the crawlers on Amazon RDS PostgreSQL instances with Multi-AZ enabled.
Provision dedicated EC2 instances running 24/7 to ensure the crawler code is always loaded in memory.
Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the maximum anticipated crawler fleet size.
Deploy the crawler tasks exclusively on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances with an automated instance diversification strategy.

questions.explanation: Spot Instances combined with fault-tolerant workload designs yield the highest possible cost savings on AWS. Short-lived batch tasks like web crawlers are ideal candidates for Spot capacity.

wrongOptionNotes.A: RDS is a relational database service, not a compute platform for running containerized crawler scripts.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Running dedicated instances 24/7 for transient jobs that execute for only a few hours daily results in extreme financial waste.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Reserved instances are financially inefficient for transient, short-lived workloads that only run a few hours a day.

questions.question: An enterprise financial reporting system generates heavy PDF reports from an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database every month-end. The report generation process spikes CPU and memory usage to 100 percent on the database instance, degrading query response times for online users. The budget does not allow upgrading the database instance class.

options.text: Migrate the database engine from PostgreSQL to Amazon DynamoDB.
Turn off automated backups and database logging during month-end processing to save CPU cycles.
Store all PDF reports directly inside Amazon EBS root volumes attached to the database.
Create an Amazon Aurora Replica and direct all heavy month-end reporting queries to the reader endpoint.

questions.explanation: Aurora Read Replicas offload heavy read-only workloads (such as month-end reporting queries) from the primary database instance, preserving performance for transactional users while adhering strictly to budget limits.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Rewriting a complex relational financial reporting application to a NoSQL key-value store requires immense engineering effort and invalidates existing relational schemas.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Disabling backups and audit logs compromises enterprise compliance and data safety standards for a minor performance gain.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Storing unstructured files in database storage or root volumes is an anti-pattern that bloats database size and increases backup times and storage costs.

questions.question: A multinational financial services company is designing a disaster recovery strategy for its core transactional database currently deployed on an Amazon Aurora MySQL database cluster in the us-east-1 Region. The business continuity requirements mandate a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of less than 1 minute and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of less than 10 minutes in the event of a regional outage. Which architectural pattern should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Set up a standard MySQL database on Amazon EC2 in us-west-2 and use native MySQL asynchronous binary log replication over a VPC peering connection.
Deploy a read replica of the Aurora cluster across Availability Zones within us-east-1 and use AWS Backup to replicate recovery points to us-west-2.
Take hourly automated snapshots of the Aurora cluster in us-east-1 and copy the snapshot to us-west-2, using an AWS Lambda function to restore the cluster during a disaster.
Configure an Aurora Global Database with a primary DB cluster in us-east-1 and a secondary DB cluster in us-west-2, enabling cross-region replication with sub-second typical latency.

questions.explanation: An Aurora Global Database is designed for globally distributed applications, allowing a single Aurora database to span multiple AWS Regions. It replicates data with no impact on database performance, uses storage-level replication with typical latencies of less than a second, and provides rapid RPO (< 1 second) and RTO (< 1 minute for local promotion, < 10 minutes for full regional switchover).

wrongOptionNotes.A: Native MySQL async replication managed manually over EC2 introduces administrative overhead, potential replication lag exceeding RPO limits during peak loads, and lacks the native multi-region failover automation of Aurora.
wrongOptionNotes.B: A read replica within us-east-1 only provides AZ-level resilience, and AWS Backup recovery point replication does not provide the sub-minute RPO required for a full regional disaster recovery.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Hourly snapshots will result in an RPO of up to 60 minutes, which severely violates the strict requirement of an RPO under 1 minute.

questions.question: An e-commerce enterprise operates a high-traffic web application deployed across the us-east-1 and us-west-2 Regions. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS service. The architecture must automatically redirect user traffic to the healthy region if the primary region experiences an outage, while maintaining weighted distribution under normal operations. Which Route 53 routing policy combination should be used?

options.text: Failover routing policy with health checks configured on the primary resource records.
Weighted routing policy combined with Route 53 health checks associated with each record.
Geolocation routing policy combined with latency-based routing policies.
Multi-value answer routing policy with DNS-based health checks.

questions.explanation: Route 53 weighted routing lets you route proportions of traffic to different resources. By associating Route 53 health checks with individual weighted records, Route 53 automatically evaluates endpoint health and routes traffic only to healthy endpoints, seamlessly handling regional failover.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Failover routing routes all traffic to the primary resource when healthy and fails over entirely to the secondary only when unhealthy. It does not support weighted traffic distribution during normal operations.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Geolocation routes based on the geographic location of the user, and mixing it directly with latency-based routing does not provide the precise weighted load distribution and automated health-check failover required.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Multi-value answer routing returns up to eight healthy records randomly and is not designed for primary/secondary weighted regional load balancing.

questions.question: A global software company is building a static web portal that must remain available even if an entire AWS Region goes offline. The architecture uses Amazon S3 for static asset storage and Amazon CloudFront for content delivery. The engineering team needs to design a multi-region active-active backend strategy for dynamic API calls handled by Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. How should the API endpoints be deployed for high availability?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with a single regional API Gateway origin and enable CloudFront standard caching.
Deploy API Gateway in the primary region with an active-passive S3 replication bucket acting as the proxy fallback.
Deploy identical API Gateway and Lambda stacks in two different AWS Regions, fronted by Route 53 latency routing with health checks.
Deploy API Gateway in a single region and configure a cross-region Network Load Balancer pointing to Lambda functions in both regions.

questions.explanation: To achieve multi-region active-active resilience for serverless APIs, identical stacks of API Gateway and Lambda must be deployed in multiple regions. Route 53 with latency or failover routing and health checks directs traffic to the operational region automatically.

wrongOptionNotes.A: A single regional API Gateway origin creates a single point of failure. If that region fails, dynamic API calls will fail regardless of CloudFront caching for static assets.
wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 replication is irrelevant to dynamic API Gateway and Lambda execution logic during a regional failure.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Network Load Balancers cannot target resources across different AWS Regions natively.

questions.question: An enterprise financial application runs on Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones in us-east-1. To prepare for disaster recovery, the organization needs to maintain a warm standby environment in eu-central-1. The database layer uses Amazon Aurora Global Database. The EC2 instances must be maintained in eu-central-1 with a minimal running capacity that can scale up rapidly during an incident. Which solution provides the most cost-effective warm standby architecture?

options.text: Configure an Auto Scaling group in eu-central-1 with a minimum capacity of zero, setting up AWS CloudFormation templates to launch instances manually when an alert triggers.
Maintain an identical Auto Scaling group in eu-central-1 configured with a minimum and maximum capacity equal to the production environment in us-east-1.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway volume in eu-central-1 that synchronizes block storage snapshots every 15 minutes from us-east-1.
Configure an Auto Scaling group in eu-central-1 with a reduced minimum and desired capacity running smaller instance sizes, and use target tracking scaling policies backed by Aurora global replicas.

questions.explanation: A warm standby disaster recovery architecture involves a smaller, scaled-down version of the production environment running continually in another region. It is more expensive than backup-and-restore but has a much lower RTO, and it is more cost-effective than an active-active multi-site setup.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Manual deployment via CloudFormation templates during a disaster introduces high RTO and human error risk, failing the requirement for rapid scaling.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Maintaining full production capacity in the standby region defeats the cost-saving purpose of a warm standby architecture, as it doubles compute costs unnecessarily.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Storage Gateway volume synchronization addresses block storage backup, not compute tier warm standby readiness for an EC2-based web application.

questions.question: A media streaming enterprise stores petabytes of video content in an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. Due to compliance mandates, all content must be replicated to an S3 bucket in us-west-2 with a maximum replication time of 15 minutes, and all replicated objects must retain their original encryption keys (AWS KMS customer managed keys). Which configuration fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to run a continuous synchronization task between the us-east-1 S3 bucket and the us-west-2 S3 bucket every 5 minutes.
Enable Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) and configure the replication rule to replicate encrypted objects using AWS KMS.
Configure standard Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) and set up an Amazon EventBridge rule to trigger an AWS Lambda function that copies newly created objects every 10 minutes.
Enable Amazon S3 Batch Replication for historical data and standard lifecycle rules for incoming objects.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) is designed for compliance requirements that necessitate predictable replication times. S3 RTC replicates 99.9% of new objects within 15 minutes and supports replica creation with AWS KMS encryption keys.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS DataSync is primarily designed for network-attached storage or periodic S3 migrations, whereas native S3 replication features built-in RTC designed precisely for inter-region bucket synchronization.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Standard S3 CRR does not guarantee a 15-minute SLA, and building a custom Lambda polling/copying mechanism introduces operational complexity and potential failure points for KMS-encrypted objects.
wrongOptionNotes.D: S3 Batch Replication is intended for replicating existing historic objects, not real-time incoming objects under a strict 15-minute SLA.

questions.question: An enterprise SaaS application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in us-east-1. The architecture needs a disaster recovery solution in us-west-2. The RPO must be near zero, and the RTO must be under 5 minutes. The database is Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Network traffic should be distributed globally with automated failover. Which architecture achieves this with the lowest complexity?

options.text: Active-Passive setup using an EC2 database replication script across regions, single ALB in us-east-1, and Route 53 DNS failover.
Active-Active setup using Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables, regional EC2 instances, and traditional public IP round-robin DNS records without health checks.
Active-Active setup using an Aurora Global Database, ALBs in both regions with EC2 Auto Scaling groups, and AWS Global Accelerator configured with endpoints in both regions.
Active-Passive setup using Route 53 simple routing, Amazon S3 static cross-region replication, and manual EC2 deployment scripts triggered by PagerDuty alerts.

questions.explanation: Combining AWS Global Accelerator, regional ALBs, Auto Scaling compute tiers, and Aurora Global Databases provides a robust, low-latency, active-active multi-region architecture that fulfills stringent RPO and RTO mandates with managed AWS services.

wrongOptionNotes.A: DNS-based failover suffers from TTL caching delays, and custom database replication scripts over WAN lack the reliability and speed of managed Aurora Global Databases.
wrongOptionNotes.B: The application runs on Aurora PostgreSQL (relational), not DynamoDB, and round-robin DNS without health checks will continuously route traffic to failed endpoints during an outage.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Manual deployment scripts and simple routing fail the RTO requirement of under 5 minutes and offer poor availability for dynamic application state.

questions.question: A global gaming company is setting up a disaster recovery environment for its user session data store. The data is currently stored in an Amazon DynamoDB table in us-east-1. The recovery site is located in eu-central-1. The business requires seamless multi-master replication with local read and write performance globally and a multi-region RPO of nearly zero. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure a DynamoDB Global Table spanning us-east-1 and eu-central-1.
Set up DynamoDB Streams in us-east-1 and trigger an AWS Lambda function in eu-central-1 to replicate items to the standby table.
Use Amazon S3 cross-region replication to synchronize DynamoDB export files dumped to S3 every hour.
Take daily point-in-time recovery (PITR) backups of the us-east-1 table and restore them automatically into eu-central-1 every night.

questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables eliminate the complexity of building and maintaining custom multi-region replication solutions. They provide automatic, multi-active replication across chosen AWS Regions, achieving sub-second replication latency.
