wrongOptionNotes.D: Migrating a relational transactional and analytical schema to NoSQL requires significant application rewriting and does not preserve complex relational reporting logic easily.

questions.question: A digital media agency hosts client web applications on Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Following a recent security incident, the engineering team notices unauthorized outbound traffic originating from several compromised EC2 instances to external malicious command-and-control servers. What combination of services should the solutions architect implement to prevent outbound exfiltration and quickly isolate affected instances cost-effectively?

options.text: Configure Amazon VPC Security Groups with strict outbound rules limiting traffic to required ports, deploy Amazon GuardDuty to detect unauthorized communications, and integrate AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to isolate instances.
Enable AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer to inspect outgoing HTTP response bodies for malicious payloads and drop active sessions automatically.
Route all outbound instance traffic through an expensive third-party hardware firewall appliance deployed in a standalone VPC peered with the application VPC.
Attach Network ACLs to every public subnet blocking all outbound traffic on port 80 and 443, and replace all EC2 instances with new ones launched from a golden AMI.

questions.explanation: Native AWS security primitives provide robust defense-in-depth. Restricting egress via Security Groups limits potential data exfiltration paths, GuardDuty detects the anomaly, and Systems Manager enables secure management.

wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS WAF inspects incoming client requests and can inspect outgoing responses, but it operates at the ALB layer and cannot block raw TCP/IP egress originating directly from compromised EC2 guest operating systems.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While third-party appliances work, they introduce unnecessary cost and architectural complexity compared to native security group egress rules and GuardDuty.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Blocking all port 80/443 traffic at the subnet Network ACL level would break legitimate web application updates and API calls for all instances in the subnet.

questions.question: An e-commerce enterprise stores high-resolution product catalog images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Recently, application performance monitoring tools detected a sharp increase in 403 Forbidden errors and soaring data transfer costs. Investigation reveals that unauthorized third-party websites are hotlinking directly to the S3 object URLs. What is the most effective and cost-efficient way to stop unauthorized hotlinking while maintaining legitimate user access?

options.text: Change the Amazon S3 bucket ACLs to private and require all legitimate users to authenticate via AWS IAM credentials before downloading any image.
Front the S3 bucket with Amazon CloudFront, enable AWS WAF or configure bucket policies enforcing the aws:Referer or aws:SourceArn condition tied to the CloudFront distribution.
Migrate all images from Amazon S3 to Amazon EBS gp3 volumes attached to an EC2 web server running an Apache .htaccess redirection module.
Enable Amazon S3 Object Ownership and enforce bucket-level cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) rules restricting GET requests to trusted domains.

questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront paired with Origin Access Control (OAC) and restricted S3 bucket policies allows you to block direct public access to S3 while seamlessly serving public assets through the CDN edge.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Requiring public shoppers to manage AWS IAM credentials or sign requests for viewing standard e-commerce product images degrades user experience unacceptably.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Moving static assets from S3 to EBS increases infrastructure cost, reduces durability, and introduces scalability bottlenecks.
wrongOptionNotes.D: CORS protects against malicious browser-based JavaScript cross-origin requests, but it does not prevent direct image hotlinking or automated scraping tools from fetching S3 objects.

questions.question: A financial technology firm runs a containerized microservices architecture on Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2 instance launch types. During heavy batch processing windows, services experience intermittent connection failures, and container logs show frequent java.net.SocketTimeoutException errors when communicating with backend databases. Network metrics reveal that the ENIs attached to the container instances are experiencing high packet drop rates due to exceeding connection tracking table limits. What is the most appropriate architectural fix?

options.text: Create multiple private subnets across additional Availability Zones and spread the container instances across them to distribute the load.
Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs in front of every internal microservice to throttle incoming connections and queue excess requests.
Migrate all microservices from Amazon ECS on EC2 to AWS Lambda without modification to eliminate network interface connection limits entirely.

Right-size the container instance types to larger Amazon EC2 instances with higher network performance limits, and tune the Linux kernel connection tracking (nf_conntrack) table size via user data scripts.

questions.explanation: When container hosts run numerous microservices, the volume of simultaneous TCP connections can exhaust the Linux kernel's connection tracking limits (`nf_conntrack`), causing silent packet drops. Tuning kernel parameters and selecting instances with appropriate network bandwidth is critical.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Spreading instances across subnets does not increase the local Linux kernel connection tracking limits on individual instance ENIs where the drops occur.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Internal microservices communicating within a private VPC do not route through API Gateway for East-West traffic; adding API Gateway adds latency and cost.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Rewriting and migrating complex Java container workloads to Lambda introduces heavy refactoring effort and does not solve underlying VPC networking constraints.

questions.question: An analytics startup stores 200 TB of raw customer telemetry data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Data engineers run daily Apache Spark jobs using Amazon EMR to query the data. Recently, query performance degraded severely, and Spark execution logs report persistent java.io.IOException errors accompanied by slow read speeds from Amazon S3. What is the most likely architectural root cause and remediation?

options.text: The EMR cluster master node has run out of disk space due to log accumulation. Remediate by attaching an Amazon EBS gp3 volume and enabling automatic log rotation.
The Amazon EMR cluster is configured across multiple Availability Zones, causing high cross-AZ data transfer latency when reading from S3.
The S3 bucket encryption keys managed via AWS KMS are experiencing API request throttling. Remediate by requesting an increase in KMS generate data key quotas.
The S3 bucket contains millions of very small files causing request rate throttling and list overhead. Remediate by compacting small files into larger Parquet or ORC files using an ETL job.

questions.explanation: The 'small files problem' is a common anti-pattern in data lakes. Compacting small files into larger columnar formats (like Parquet) drastically improves Amazon S3 throughput and big data query performance.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Master node disk space issues cause job scheduling failures or YARN ResourceManager crashes rather than direct I/O read errors from S3.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Reading data from Amazon S3 from within the same region does not incur cross-AZ data transfer fees or latency penalties based on EMR node subnet placement.
wrongOptionNotes.C: KMS throttling typically results in explicit AccessDenied or KMS throttling exceptions in logs, rather than general I/O read exceptions during Spark processing.

questions.question: A healthcare provider operates a patient records application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Bouncer. Compliance auditors flag that during unexpected regional outages or failovers, unencrypted health records traverse public AWS service endpoints when accessing Amazon DynamoDB. What architectural change must the solutions architect implement to ensure data-in-transit remains strictly within the AWS private network backbone?

options.text: Deploy NAT Gateways in every Availability Zone and route all outbound database traffic through elastic IP addresses.
Configure Amazon VPC Gateway Endpoints for Amazon DynamoDB in the VPC routing tables, ensuring traffic to DynamoDB remains internal to the AWS network.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the application VPC back to the on-premises data center and route all DynamoDB API calls through the corporate firewall.
Enable TLS 1.3 encryption on all Application Load Bouncer listener rules and enforce HTTPS for all backend database connections.

questions.explanation: VPC Endpoints (Gateway type for DynamoDB and S3; Interface type for most other services) ensure that traffic between your VPC and supported AWS services stays within the Amazon private network, enhancing security and compliance.

wrongOptionNotes.A: NAT Gateways route traffic over the public internet space via AWS edge routers, failing the requirement to keep traffic entirely within private network constructs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Routing AWS service calls through an on-premises data center via VPN introduces massive latency, egress data costs, and a single point of failure.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While TLS encrypts traffic between clients and the ALB, it does not secure the traffic path from EC2 instances to public AWS service endpoints unless VPC endpoints are utilized.

questions.question: An online ticketing platform experiences sudden traffic surges during popular event sales. The architecture uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database backend. During these peaks, the database experiences high connection counts and CPU spikes, resulting in connection refused errors for the web application servers. Which architecture pattern offers the most scalable and cost-effective relief for read-heavy database bottlenecks?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database to cache frequently accessed catalog and event data, and direct read queries to the cache.
Upgrade the Amazon RDS MySQL database instance to the largest available memory-optimized instance type and enable multi-AZ high availability.
Implement Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on all database backup snapshots to speed up replication times across regions.
Migrate the MySQL database tables to Amazon EBS io2 Block Express volumes with maximum provisioned IOPS to accelerate query execution.

questions.explanation: Introducing an in-memory caching layer using Amazon ElastiCache offloads repetitive read queries from the relational database, drastically reducing connection counts and CPU utilization during peak traffic.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Vertical scaling is expensive, has an upper hardware ceiling, and does not fundamentally solve high concurrent connection exhaustion during traffic surges.
wrongOptionNotes.C: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up file uploads to S3 over wide-area networks, which is entirely irrelevant to live database connection and CPU exhaustion.
wrongOptionNotes.D: The bottleneck is CPU utilization and connection pool limits under high concurrency, not underlying storage IOPS limitations.

questions.question: An enterprise financial application runs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Bouncer. Users report intermittent 502 Bad Gateway errors. CloudWatch metrics indicate that the ALB target group has zero healthy hosts during specific scaling events. Upon inspection, new instances are failing health checks immediately upon launch because the application deployment script takes 5 minutes to complete. What is the most efficient architectural remediation?

options.text: Modify the Auto Scaling group cooldown period to 2 hours and set the scaling policy metric evaluation period to 60 minutes.
Replace the Application Load Bouncer with a Network Load Bouncer and disable health checks entirely to allow all instances to receive traffic regardless of initialization status.
Migrate the application from Amazon EC2 to AWS Lambda and invoke functions directly from the Application Load Bouncer.
Configure ALB Target Group health check grace periods and increase the health check startup threshold, while baking the application code into a golden AMI using EC2 Image Builder.

questions.explanation: Using golden AMIs minimizes runtime bootstrap tasks, ensuring faster instance readiness. Additionally, configuring appropriate ALB health check grace periods ensures Auto Scaling instances are not prematurely terminated before the application is fully online.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Extending cooldown periods does not solve the root cause of instances failing health checks during startup; it only slows down the scaling reaction time.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Disabling health checks is dangerous because it sends traffic to failed or uninitialized instances, resulting in broken user experiences.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While Lambda avoids instance management, rewriting a complex enterprise EC2 application to serverless functions solely to bypass startup health check tuning is impractical.

questions.question: A global news agency stores a massive archive of digital video footage in Amazon S3. Editors need to search and retrieve specific clips based on metadata tags. Recently, search queries have failed with 503 Slow Down errors, and data retrieval costs have skyrocketed. The S3 bucket receives thousands of concurrent PUT and GET requests on the same naming prefix. What architectural change should be implemented to optimize performance and cost?

options.text: Upgrade the S3 storage class from Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically archive inactive clips without manual lifecycle rules.
Attach Amazon EBS provisioned IOPS volumes to an EC2 proxy fleet that sits in front of the S3 bucket to handle incoming search requests.
Enable Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy all video assets to a secondary AWS Region to split read traffic evenly across regions.
Implement randomized hash prefixes or unique identifiers on S3 object key names to distribute requests across multiple partitions, and transition older footage to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 automatically scales to support high request rates, but it does so across prefixes. Monotonically increasing prefixes (like timestamps or sequential IDs) concentrate traffic onto single partitions, causing 503 errors. Adding randomized hash prefixes solves this.

wrongOptionNotes.A: While Intelligent-Tiering helps with unpredictable access patterns, it does not solve high-frequency request rate throttling on single prefixes caused by poor naming conventions.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Placing an EC2 proxy in front of S3 adds cost, complexity, and a new bottleneck without solving S3's underlying prefix scaling design.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Replication duplicates storage costs and does not resolve partition request throttling on hot prefixes within a single bucket namespace.

questions.question: An analytics enterprise operates a data warehouse on Amazon Redshift consisting of 4 dc2.large nodes. The query volume has tripled over the last month, and users report that complex executive dashboards are timing out. The cluster CPU utilization is consistently at 99%. What is the most cost-effective architectural solution to restore dashboard performance?

options.text: Increase the Amazon Redshift backup retention period from 7 days to 30 days to allow automated cluster snapshots to reindex tables.
Enable Amazon Redshift Concurrency Scaling to automatically add cluster capacity during peak query loads, and optimize heavy query sort and distribution keys.
Export all data from Amazon Redshift to Amazon S3 and query the data directly using Amazon Athena without maintaining a data warehouse.
Migrate the entire Amazon Redshift cluster immediately to the largest ra3.16xlarge node type with managed storage.

questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift Concurrency Scaling is designed specifically to handle unpredictable, concurrent read query spikes automatically and cost-effectively without manual cluster intervention.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Backup retention periods have no impact on query execution performance, dashboard timeouts, or node CPU utilization.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Rewiring mission-critical executive dashboards from Redshift to Athena requires rebuilding all SQL views, tuning, and BI integrations, which is disruptive and unnecessary.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Migrating to the largest node type is vastly over-provisioned and expensive when Concurrency Scaling can handle transient spikes cost-effectively.

questions.question: A financial services firm runs a mission-critical billing application on Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon EBS gp2 volumes. During peak end-of-month processing, application logs display severe I/O latency spikes and IOPS throttling warnings. The root cause is identified as exhausted burst balance on the EBS volumes. What is the most cost-effective and immediate architectural remediation?

options.text: Modify the Amazon EBS volumes in place from gp2 to gp3, provisioning baseline IOPS and throughput independently of storage capacity.
Stop the EC2 instances, take a snapshot of the volumes, and increase the size of the gp2 volumes to 16 TiB to artificially increase burst capacity.
Detach the gp2 volumes and attach Amazon EBS io2 Block Express volumes with maximum provisioned IOPS to all EC2 instances.
Migrate the application data from EBS volumes to local instance store storage attached to the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation: Amazon EBS gp2 performance is tied directly to volume size, leading to exhausted burst balances on smaller volumes under heavy loads. Migrating to gp3 decouples IOPS and throughput from storage size, delivering consistent performance at a lower cost.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Over-provisioning gp2 storage solely to gain burst IOPS is inefficient and expensive compared to migrating to gp3 volumes.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While io2 Block Express provides extreme performance, it is significantly more expensive and often overkill when gp3 can easily meet the workload requirements cost-effectively.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Instance store storage is ephemeral and data is lost when an instance stops or terminates, making it unsuitable for persistent financial billing records.

questions.question: An enterprise organization manages multiple AWS accounts using AWS Organizations. The cloud security team discovers that several development accounts have disabled Amazon GuardDuty and deleted default AWS CloudTrail trails, violating corporate compliance mandates. What architectural mechanism should the solutions architect implement to enforce compliance and prevent accounts from disabling core security services?

options.text: Implement AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) denying the permission to disable GuardDuty or modify CloudTrail, and configure AWS GuardDuty delegated administrator features with auto-enablement across the organization.
Deploy an Amazon CloudWatch alarm in each member account that sends an email notification to the IT helpdesk whenever GuardDuty is disabled.
Create IAM user accounts with AdministratorAccess in every member account and manually audit compliance logs weekly via a custom bash script.
Attach Amazon VPC Security Groups to the root AWS account blocking all API calls destined for GuardDuty and CloudTrail endpoints.

questions.explanation: AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) provide central guardrails by setting permission boundaries for member accounts, ensuring foundational security services like GuardDuty and CloudTrail cannot be disabled.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Notifications alert teams after an infraction occurs, but they do not actively prevent or block non-compliant actions the way SCPs do.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Manual audits and sharing high-privilege IAM users across accounts violates security best practices and does not prevent accidental or malicious configuration drift.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Security Groups operate at the EC2 instance and ENI level within a VPC; they cannot block global AWS API control plane actions.

questions.question: A digital streaming platform caches high-resolution video thumbnails using Amazon CloudFront backed by an Application Load Bouncer and Amazon ECS containers. Following a recent deployment, users worldwide report seeing broken or outdated thumbnails. Inspection reveals that the backend application updated image files without changing their filenames, and CloudFront is serving stale cached assets. What is the most operationally efficient and cost-effective way to fix the stale cache issue?

options.text: Implement cache-control headers with appropriate max-age directives in the backend application responses and use CloudFront Cache Policies to respect origin headers.
Execute a CloudFront cache invalidation for the entire wildcard path (/*) every time a new container task starts up.
Delete and recreate the CloudFront distribution from scratch during each software deployment pipeline run.
Disable caching entirely on the CloudFront distribution so every client request forwards directly to the ECS container backend.

questions.explanation: Proper cache control headers and CloudFront cache policies provide precise control over content freshness. Versioning assets or respecting origin expiration headers prevents stale content without incurring costly invalidations.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Wildcard invalidations frequently can become expensive and hit CloudFront invalidation quotas rapidly if executed repeatedly on every deployment.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Recreating distributions causes prolonged downtime, changes DNS endpoints, and disrupts global edge caching entirely.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Bypassing the CDN entirely removes caching benefits, resulting in massive backend compute load and soaring data egress costs.

questions.question: A financial services company runs a multi-tier web application on Amazon EC2 instances inside a private subnet. The application instances require daily software patches downloaded from an external repository on the public internet, but security compliance strictly forbids assigning public IPv4 addresses or exposing inbound ports to the instances. Which architectural pattern meets these security and compliance requirements while optimizing cost?

options.text: Attach a public IPv4 address and an Internet Gateway directly to the private EC2 instances.
Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, and configure the private subnet route table to direct outbound internet traffic to the NAT Gateway.
Configure an AWS Transfer Family server in the private subnet to act as an outbound proxy.
Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to route all EC2 internet traffic back through the corporate data center.

questions.explanation: To allow private instances to reach the public internet securely for updates without exposing them to inbound connections, a NAT Gateway placed in a public subnet with routing configured from the private subnet is the standard, cost-optimized AWS best practice.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Attaching public IP addresses violates the security requirement forbidding public IP addresses on internal application instances.
wrongOptionNotes.C: AWS Transfer Family is designed for managed file transfers (SFTP, FTPS, FTP) and cannot act as a general HTTP/HTTPS outbound patch proxy.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Routing all patch download traffic through a corporate data center creates unnecessary data transfer costs and a severe architectural bottleneck.

questions.question: An enterprise runs a sensitive data processing pipeline on Amazon EC2 instances. Compliance mandates that all Amazon EBS data volumes attached to these instances must be encrypted at rest using a custom KMS key managed by the security team. A solutions architect needs to automate this requirement across all newly launched instances. What is the most secure and cost-effective way to enforce this?

options.text: Configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling launch templates with EBS volume encryption enabled by default and specify the customer managed KMS key.
Deploy an AWS Lambda function that monitors CloudTrail logs for EC2 launches and detaches volumes if they are unencrypted.
Write a custom cron script on each EC2 instance that runs hourly to encrypt unencrypted EBS volumes using the AWS CLI.
Rely entirely on default AWS account-level EBS encryption settings without specifying a customer managed KMS key.

questions.explanation: Enforcing encryption at launch via EC2 launch templates and Auto Scaling configurations ensures proactive compliance without risking runtime failures or requiring complex post-launch remediation scripts.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Detaching volumes post-launch is reactive and will crash the operating system or corrupt data, violating reliability and availability goals.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Root volumes cannot be encrypted on the fly via scripts while the instance is running, and secondary volume re-encryption scripts introduce operational complexity and race conditions.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Account-level default encryption uses the AWS managed key (aws/ebs), which does not satisfy the specific compliance requirement for a customer managed key.

questions.question: An e-commerce company stores sensitive customer payment logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Due to regulatory frameworks, objects in this bucket must be protected against accidental deletion or modification by any user, including root account credentials, for a mandatory retention period of 3 years. Which S3 feature should the solutions architect configure?

options.text: Apply an S3 bucket policy that denies the s3:DeleteObject action to all IAM users and roles except the security administrator.
Enable AWS CloudTrail data events and configure Amazon SNS alerts whenever an object is deleted.
Enable S3 Versioning and configure lifecycle rules to expire current versions after 3 years.
Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period of 3 years.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode enforces a Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) model where not even the root account can delete or alter the data until the retention period expires.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Bucket policies can be modified or deleted by users with administrative permissions, and they do not prevent root account modifications or fulfill strict immutable compliance requirements.
wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudTrail and SNS provide auditing and notification capabilities, but they are detective controls that do not prevent unauthorized deletion.
wrongOptionNotes.C: S3 Versioning with lifecycle expiration allows users with proper permissions to delete object versions or remove markers, which does not provide write-once-read-many (WORM) immutability protection.

questions.question: A healthcare startup stores patient medical records in Amazon S3. The security team discovers that authorized data analysts are occasionally copying sensitive files to their personal AWS accounts. To prevent data exfiltration while maintaining legitimate internal data access, what is the most cost-effective and secure guardrail to implement?

options.text: Attach an IAM policy to every analyst user that explicitly denies access to all external S3 buckets.
Implement an S3 bucket policy that evaluates theaws:PrincipalOrgID or aws:ResourceAccount condition to restrict access to trusted internal principals.
Enable VPC Flow Logs on all VPCs and inspect them manually for unauthorized data transfers.
Deploy Amazon GuardDuty and configure automated remediation scripts to delete AWS accounts that access company S3 buckets.

questions.explanation: Resource-based S3 bucket policies combined with organizational condition keys provide a robust, preventative boundary guardrail against cross-account data exfiltration.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Managing explicit denies across hundreds of individual IAM policies is difficult to maintain and does not prevent users from using external accounts to pull data if they have rogue credential access.
wrongOptionNotes.C: VPC Flow Logs do not capture S3 API calls (as S3 traffic bypasses standard EC2 ENI packet inspection in many configurations) and manual inspection is a reactive control.
wrongOptionNotes.D: GuardDuty is a threat detection service, and automatically deleting external AWS accounts is unfeasible and destructive.

questions.question: A financial enterprise uses AWS Organizations to manage 50 separate AWS accounts. The corporate security team requires that all Amazon RDS database instances across every account must be encrypted with a centralized KMS key managed by the security account. How can the solutions architect enforce this globally with minimal operational overhead?

options.text: Rely on default AWS account configurations by sending an email notification to account owners each month.
Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the organization root or organizational unit level that denies the creation of unencrypted RDS instances.
Configure AWS Trusted Advisor alerts to notify the security team whenever an unencrypted RDS instance is launched.
Write an AWS Lambda function in each account that periodically scans for RDS instances and encrypts them in place.

questions.explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations are preventive controls that enforce compliance across multiple accounts without requiring distributed scripts or manual oversight.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Email notifications are reactive and rely on human compliance rather than automated security enforcement.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Trusted Advisor provides detective alerts after the fact, violating the requirement to prevent unencrypted databases from being launched.
wrongOptionNotes.D: RDS instances cannot be encrypted in-place if they were launched unencrypted; creating snapshots, copying with encryption, and restoring adds extreme operational complexity and downtime.

questions.question: An enterprise web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The security team mandates that all traffic between the ALB and the backend EC2 instances must be fully authenticated, authorized, and encrypted using TLS. Which configuration satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Install AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) public certificates directly onto the guest operating systems of the EC2 instances.
Configure the ALB target group protocol to HTTP and rely on internal VPC isolation for security.
Configure the ALB target group protocol to HTTPS, install valid certificates on the EC2 instances, and configure security groups to allow traffic on port 443.
Terminate TLS at the ALB and use TCP passthrough directly to port 80 on the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation: End-to-end encryption requires TLS termination at the load balancer and re-encryption via HTTPS target groups communicating directly with HTTPS listeners on the backend EC2 instances.

wrongOptionNotes.A: ACM public certificates cannot be exported or installed directly onto private EC2 instances; they can only be used on integrated AWS services like ALBs and CloudFront.
wrongOptionNotes.B: HTTP traffic between the ALB and EC2 instances is unencrypted in transit, failing the encryption compliance mandate.
wrongOptionNotes.D: TCP passthrough bypasses ALB certificate handling and leaves backend communication unencrypted unless application-layer TLS is configured separately.

questions.question: A software company is building a multi-tenant SaaS application on AWS. Each tenant's data must be completely isolated within Amazon DynamoDB. The application uses AWS STS to assume tenant-specific IAM roles. Which DynamoDB feature should the solutions architect leverage to enforce item-level least privilege access based on the authenticated tenant?

options.text: Use IAM policy condition keys such as dynamodb:LeadingKeys to restrict users to accessing only items where the partition key matches their tenant ID.
Attach an Amazon S3 bucket policy to the DynamoDB table to restrict row-level access.
Create a separate DynamoDB table for every tenant in the system.
Write custom middleware in the application code to filter out unauthorized rows before returning data to the client.

questions.explanation: DynamoDB fine-grained access control using IAM condition keys like `dynamodb:LeadingKeys` allows secure multi-tenancy within a single table without relying entirely on application-layer filtering.

wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 bucket policies apply to Amazon S3 resources, not Amazon DynamoDB tables.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Creating a separate table per tenant is cost-inefficient, hits AWS account table limits quickly, and does not leverage DynamoDB's built-in fine-grained access control.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Relying solely on application-layer filtering violates the defense-in-depth principle because a software bug could expose cross-tenant data.

questions.question: An organization requires that all Amazon S3 buckets created across all AWS accounts must have default encryption enabled, public access blocked, and server access logging turned on. The cloud architecture team wants an automated remediation mechanism that immediately corrects non-compliant buckets upon creation without human intervention.

options.text: Rely on AWS Trusted Advisor console checks to highlight unencrypted buckets during quarterly audits.
Attach an IAM group policy to all developers restricting their ability to use the S3 console.
Send a daily email report via Amazon SNS to developers listing non-compliant buckets.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that triggers an AWS Lambda function upon the S3 CreateBucket API call to apply security configurations automatically.

questions.explanation: EventBridge combined with AWS Lambda provides a robust, event-driven remediation pattern for enforcing compliance settings immediately after resource creation.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Quarterly audits are far too slow for proactive security guardrails in modern cloud environments.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Restricting console access does not prevent programmatic creation of non-compliant buckets via CLI or infrastructure-as-code tools.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Email reports are detective and rely on manual developer action, which fails the requirement for immediate, automated remediation.

questions.question: A financial institution runs a core banking application on Amazon EC2 instances. Security auditors mandate that any modification to security groups, network ACLs, or IAM policies must trigger an immediate, high-priority alert to the security operations team. Which AWS service combination provides this capability with the lowest operational overhead?

options.text: AWS CloudTrail to log API calls, Amazon EventBridge to filter security-relevant events, and Amazon SNS to dispatch immediate alerts.
Amazon CloudWatch logs agent installed on every EC2 instance parsing /var/log/secure for security modifications.
AWS Config rules evaluated on a 24-hour cycle backed by custom Athena queries.
AWS Trusted Advisor weekly batch scans checking for IAM and VPC misconfigurations.

questions.explanation: The native serverless integration of CloudTrail, EventBridge, and SNS provides real-time detection and alerting for AWS control plane modifications without managing infrastructure.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Security groups, NACLs, and IAM policies are managed via AWS control plane APIs, not local Linux log files on EC2 instances.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Evaluation cycles of 24 hours are too slow for real-time security alerting.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Weekly batch scans do not provide the real-time alerting required for critical security configuration changes.

questions.question: A retail corporation hosts a public web application behind Amazon CloudFront. The security team discovers that the backend Application Load Balancer is receiving direct HTTP requests from unauthorized external IP addresses that bypass CloudFront. How can the solutions architect secure the ALB so that it ONLY accepts traffic originating from CloudFront?

options.text: Attach an IAM user policy to the Application Load Balancer.
Enable Amazon S3 block public access on the Application Load Balancer target groups.
Configure CloudFront Origin Request Headers with a secret custom header, and configure an ALB listener rule to drop any request missing that header.
Modify the ALB security group to allow inbound traffic from all public IP addresses.

questions.explanation: To prevent direct access to an ALB behind CloudFront, architects use custom origin headers evaluated by ALB rules or restrict ALB security groups using AWS managed prefix lists for CloudFront.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Application Load Balancers do not support attaching IAM user policies for network-level access control.
wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 block public access applies exclusively to Amazon S3 buckets, not ALB target groups.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Allowing all public IP addresses on the ALB security group directly permits the exact vulnerability being described (bypassing CloudFront).

questions.question: An enterprise developer needs administrative access to AWS resources for debugging purposes. However, corporate compliance dictates that no user can have permanent administrative privileges. Instead, developers must assume an IAM role that grants full administrator access, but the session must automatically expire after exactly 1 hour and require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). How should this be configured?

options.text: Configure the IAM role trust policy with a maximum session duration of 1 hour (3600 seconds) and include a condition requiring aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent.
Configure an Amazon S3 bucket policy with a time-based condition to restrict developer actions.
Attach an inline policy to the developer user that explicitly denies administrative actions after 60 minutes using a cron job.
Rely on the AWS root user account credentials shared securely among developers via a password manager.

questions.explanation: IAM role trust policies support maximum session duration constraints (up to 12 hours) and conditional checks for multi-factor authentication, enforcing least-privilege temporary access.

wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 bucket policies govern S3 data operations, not IAM role assumption or administrative AWS API access.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on custom cron jobs to modify user policies is fragile and insecure; session duration should be governed natively by IAM session limits.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Sharing root account credentials violates every foundational security best practice and compliance standard (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC2).

questions.question: An analytics company is storing sensitive customer personally identifiable information (PII) in Amazon S3. The security team requires that all data objects must be encrypted at rest using keys managed entirely by the company within AWS KMS, with strict auditing of every key usage. Which encryption configuration meets these criteria?

options.text: Use Server-Side Encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
Rely on client-side plaintext storage with HTTPS transport layer security.
Enable Amazon S3 Glacier Vault Lock without encryption parameters.
Configure S3 bucket default encryption using AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) with a customer managed KMS key (CMK).

questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with customer managed keys provides full cryptographic control, key rotation management, and detailed audit logs via AWS CloudTrail for sensitive workloads.

wrongOptionNotes.A: SSE-S3 uses AWS-managed master keys stored and managed entirely by S3 behind the scenes, providing no customer visibility or control over key policies.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Storing data unencrypted at rest violates PII compliance mandates regardless of transport encryption.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Vault Lock enforces compliance retention policies but does not handle data encryption at rest.

questions.question: An engineering team is deploying a serverless microservices application using AWS Lambda functions. Each Lambda function connects to a different database depending on its environment (staging or production). The database passwords must be stored securely, rotated automatically every 30 days, and retrieved dynamically by the Lambda functions without hardcoding secrets in source code. What is the most secure and cost-effective AWS service combination?

options.text: Store database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled via a Lambda template, and grant the Lambda execution role permissions to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.
Hardcode credentials into an Amazon S3 bucket with public read access enabled for internal debugging.
Store database credentials in plaintext configuration files bundled directly inside the Lambda deployment package.
Store passwords as environment variables in plaintext within the AWS Lambda configuration console.

questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager natively supports automated secret rotation and secure retrieval via IAM policies, eliminating hardcoded credentials.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Exposing database credentials in a publicly accessible S3 bucket represents a critical security breach.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Hardcoding credentials in deployment packages exposes secrets to anyone with read access to the code repository and violates security standards.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Environment variables are visible in plaintext in the AWS console and API responses unless encrypted with custom KMS keys, and they do not support automated rotation.

questions.question: A financial enterprise operates multiple AWS accounts. The security team needs a centralized view of security alerts, misconfigurations, and threat intelligence findings across all accounts without manually logging into each individual AWS console. Which native AWS service configuration provides this centralized visibility?

options.text: Designate a security management account as the delegated administrator for Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, and Amazon Macie, and link all member accounts.
Export VPC Flow Logs from every account into a single public Amazon S3 bucket.
Share the root account credentials of all member accounts with the central security team.
Write a custom AWS Lambda function in each member account that emails alerts to the central security team's inbox.

questions.explanation: Multi-account AWS security tooling uses delegated administrators in services like Security Hub and GuardDuty to aggregate findings into a single pane of glass.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Public S3 buckets expose sensitive network traffic logs to the internet, and network logs alone do not provide aggregated security findings or threat intelligence.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Sharing root credentials violates basic security principles and compliance frameworks.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Emailing raw alerts from individual accounts creates administrative overhead, lacks centralized dashboard aggregation, and is difficult to manage.

questions.question: An enterprise organization requires that all Amazon EBS volumes attached to Amazon EC2 instances must be automatically encrypted by default across all regions in a newly provisioned AWS account. What is the most operationally efficient way to enforce this baseline security setting?

options.text: Write an AWS CloudFormation custom resource for every single EC2 stack to explicitly declare encryption parameters.
Configure an Amazon SNS topic to alert administrators whenever an unencrypted volume is created.
Enable EBS encryption by default in the EC2 console for each region within the account.
Attach an IAM policy to all developers forbidding them from launching EC2 instances.

questions.explanation: Enabling EBS encryption by default at the account level in each active region ensures automatic, foolproof encryption for all subsequent volume creations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Relying on template-level declarations is prone to human error if developers write templates without the custom resource, whereas account-level defaults provide an automatic baseline.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Alerting is reactive and does not prevent unencrypted volumes from being provisioned.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Forbidding developers from launching instances halts business operations entirely, rather than securing the configuration.
